News.title: Inside Britain’s unfriendliest town with Buzzballz at breakfast, teen raids on Greggs & brazen thieves as young as 10
News.content:
WATCHING the busy commuters bustle by, an unwashed man polishes off his second 13.5 per cent BuzzBallz vodka cocktail of the morning – and it’s only 8.20am.

A street away, a homeless lady cuddles a Paddington Bear toy as she sleeps among a three-metre pile of clothes and market traders brace themselves for another day combatting thieves as young as 10.



Welcome to the East London borough of Barking and Dagenham, which has just been named the ‘unfriendliest place’ in the UK, according to a Government community life survey of residents.



It scored a measly eight out of 100 on the poll’s Connection Barometer – a collective total of ratings based on questions like belonging, loneliness, pride in the area and trust of fellow locals. The ‘most friendly’ spot, the Isles of Scilly, scored 99.

Among the most damning responses was that just 21.1 per cent of locals trusted their neighbours and only 42.8 per cent were proud to live there – the average score was nearly 60 per cent.

Surprisingly, during The Sun’s visit to Barking, locals seemed to agree with their new unsavoury title. Three described the area as “a s***hole” and one insisted the only route for redemption would be “to burn it down and start again”.

Having already seen a street drinker downing beverages from 8am and several spots where homeless people sleep among mounds of clothing and broken down cardboard boxes, the town soon starts to come alive.

But perhaps living up to the ‘unfriendly’ title, few shoppers in the market are willing to stop and talk.



“I haven’t got time” and “I’m in a rush” are among the excuses. Others pretend they haven’t heard my question and one woman yells “No” while rolling her eyes.

Nearby a retired jeweller, 67, who didn’t want to be named, tensely grips her handbag with both hands as she warns: “Watch out, they will pinch anything.”

She tries to race in and out of Barking as quickly as she can, claiming the area is blighted by gangs of pickpockets, who act in groups of 10.

“I’ve been here for 28 years too long,” she adds. “It’s a s***hole. People are rude. If you smile at someone, they won’t smile back.”

Zara Hussain, 31, who just gave birth a month ago, says her mum warned her about carrying a bag while going into town, fearing “a daylight robbery”.



“If you look nice amongst s*** you’re going to get robbed,” she says. “It’s not that you’re asking for it but it happens.”

The lifelong Barking resident claims her home has been burgled three times in the last 15 years. Even her Ring Doorbell, which films people, hasn’t deterred them.

But defiantly, she adds: “We’re not leaving Barking because it’s our home. This is where my heart is. It’s rundown, it’s s*** but it’s home.”

Zara believes the area is in dire need of gentrification and dreams of a Westfield-style shopping centre being built here.

“People are pretty miserable here, given what’s happening in their financial situations there’s nothing for them to look forward to that’s free, other than the sun,” she adds.



Mum-of-three Anne Read, 63, disagrees, believing more investment would only lead to “more vandalism” and trouble and wouldn’t reduce the problems.

She says: “I live nearby and they painted an area up. It really did look nice. It lasted two weeks. There was graffiti and homeless drug addicts s***ting on the stairs. It was disgusting.

“Barking is terrible, nothing will change, unless you burn it down and start again. The police sirens start from 6.30am, they are out before the birds.”

Anne recalls the house of her neighbour, who died from cancer three years ago, being left vacant for a few weeks and one day she spotted an addict “smoking a crack pipe in her porch”.

The area, she complains, is also blighted by “mad shoplifters” and so many pickpocket gangs that she refuses to visit the town centre without her niece.



“It’s a s***hole now,” Anne says. “People aren’t friendly because they are scared to be. If they are, they will be mugged. It’s terrible.”

She recalls once bending down to tie an old lady’s shoelaces for her, fearing she would fall over, only to be told by the pensioner: “Oh, I thought you were going to mug me.”

Ann adds: “It’s so bad that my one son moved to Durham to get away from here, my daughter fled to Norfolk and my other son, in Dagenham, is desperate to leave too.”

By 10am, four new street drinkers have emerged. Glugging Guinness, shots of spirits and Gen-Z favourite BuzzBallz cocktails, one yells “10 drinks… solid” before clinking cans with a pal.

Now Barking’s market, which sells everything from electricals and perfumes to bargain bucket clothes for as little as a fiver, is brimming with shoppers.



Learning against a hotel fire exit is a lady busily scratching her fourth scratchcard of the day and in the distance, weaving in and out of the crowds, are two teenage boys also hoping to get lucky.

Walking with swagger, pace and purpose, they mutter to each other before darting into a Greggs bakery.



Seconds later they emerge, carrying a bounty of baguettes, chicken bites and fizzy drinks. With smirks on their faces, they race away and around the corner.

There, one of them asks a takeaway food truck owner for a fork and then greedily scoffs down his stolen treats while stifling his laughter.

“It happens all the time, young and old,” a Greggs worker tells us and claims they are regular shoplifters.

But their raids may not last for long, as the employee says they have security cameras that automatically photographs thieves and sends the images to the police.



According to CrimeRate, Baking and Dagenham had the worst crime rate for robbery in the whole of London in March last year, with 116 incidents reported.

Back then it was also the Capital’s most dangerous area for violence and sexual offences, with 676 crimes. However in 2026, its crime rates have dropped, now 1.5 per cent lower than the London average.

But those stats are of no comfort to mum-of-two Georgia Douglas, 30, who insists the area is “no longer safe for kids”.

She believes their ‘unfriendly’ title is fair, due to strangers “reacting so aggressively” while passing one another in the street.

“In my lifetime, it has gotten worse,” she says. “You have stabbings, gangs, paedophiles and women getting raped. You’ve got to protect your children.”



Another passerby chimes in: “Here it’s full of pickpocketing, knifing, people killing one another left, right and centre. I try to get in and out as quickly as I can.”

Georgia claims gangs are targeting 13 and 14 year olds and teaching them sneaky ploys to sell drugs on the street.

“They come up to you and say, ‘Oh, I recognise you’ and they will ask, ‘Do you smoke weed?’” she adds.

Taka Chigodora, 56, who moved here from Zimbabwe in 2004, knows this world personally because a teenage family member was lured into a gang.

“A lot of people I know believe raising children in Barking and Dagenham is one of the worst things you can do,” the social worker says.



“A female teenager I know got involved in gangs and ended up in prison. When young people grow up they want a sense of belonging and gangs offer that.

“She got offered things that are not lawful. There was drug selling. When they are doing this they want to protect themselves so carry knives and weapons.”

Yet, Taka insists he feels safe and before speaking to us was – perhaps boldly, considering the issues with thieves – waving his bank card around with his hand.



Nearby Terry, 40, tells us: “There used to be a lot of crimes going on – drug use, selling drugs, people fighting – but it’s reducing, it’s getting calmer and more friendly.”

However, he admits he “doesn’t hang around at night” because of the potential for trouble and lists one of the best things about the area as the transport links “to get out of here”.

In spite of the ‘unfriendliness’ findings, the market traders seem to be a strong community – often watching over each other’s stalls and working together to chase down thieves.

They are used to the panicked yells of “stop”, “he’s got it” or “someone’s taken” whatever item they have nicked. Most refused to be named, fearing reprisals.

“This is one of the worst places in the country for stealing,” says one, who has spent 20 years tolling here.



“You always see people running and it’s because they have stolen something from a trader.”

He recalls one incident just last week, where a lady was unloading her stock. She turned around and in seconds an e-bike rider had raced up, snatched her bag and sped away.

“That’s what we’re up against,” he says. “They see female traders as especially easy targets and aren’t afraid to pull out a knife.

“Police try their best but by the time they get there, the thief is off. The advent of electric scooters and bikes has been major.”

The Sun did see three separate police patrols during our visit – although two officers looked more intent on their Greggs’ sausage rolls than looking out for crime.



Another market trader, 24, claims the thieves, who strike “every single day”, often work in gangs and are getting ever-younger.

“You’ll be serving the adult and their kids are nicking,” he says. “They are teaching them this, some are as young as 10.

“It’s terrible, they don’t care any more. No one has any money now, but a lot are stealing because they want to.

“They are terrible. It’s a nightmare and it happens every day. You have a set few, who try it regularly. They are wrong’uns.”

Things are so bad, he claims, that his uncle’s car was broken into for his disability parking permit. Now he uses a steering wheel lock, not only for the steering wheel but the Blue Badge too.



'We take these concerns seriouslys,' says cops Acting Superintendent Mo Mahmood, of the Met Police, told us: “We take these concerns seriously and are committed to tackling the issues that matter most to local people.” They say better use of technology and improved information sharing continues to help them identify and bring repeat offenders to justice. Their neighbourhood policing teams “work closely” with the council, business and community partners to “maintain a visible presence, target persistent re-offenders and focus activity where it is most needed”. Act Supt Mahmood adds: “Our officers will continue to patrol key town centre locations, engage with businesses and residents and tackle antisocial behaviour.” The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham Council told us: “We recognise there are challenges in Barking and Dagenham, but we have a clear plan and we’re making strong progress to improve life for residents. “We are very proud of the strong sense of community that exists across Barking and Dagenham and do not believe the description of our borough as the ‘least friendly place to live’ reflects the reality of life here. “From delivering cleaner and safer streets, improving neighbourhoods, building new homes, supporting local businesses and investing in opportunities for young people, we’re focused on making our borough an even better place to live. “Through our It Starts Here campaign and wider work with residents, community groups and local partners, we are continuing to build on that progress and make Barking and Dagenham a place everyone is proud of.”

“I mean, who nicks from the disabled?” he adds, shaking his head.

Govin Rai, 24, who has run his father’s stall for 15 years, admits they are “fortunate to have a couple of workers to keep an eye out” for thieves but still stock goes missing.

“We mostly go after thieves but it depends on how much you’re losing, how busy you are and what the risk of chasing them is,” he adds. “Is your life worth a fiver?”

He believes social clubs or sports teams could curb youngsters’ bad behaviour and encourage more inclusion among adults in times when “everyone is glued to their phones”.



Currently Barking and Dagenham is more deprived than 97 per cent of English local authorities, yet has spawned many talented people in the past.

There have been Three Lions footballers Bobby Moore, Sir Alf Ramsey and John Terry, EastEnders’ hardman Ross Kemp, Shaun of the Dead’s Nick Frost and 1967 Eurovision Song Contest winner Sandie Shaw.

But now, locals are desperate for change – more investment in services, increased police patrols and rejuvenation to its rundown sections.

If that happens, it may finally put a smile back on the faces of residents from England’s “least friendly” borough.

News.title: ‘Obsessed’ teacher, 45, sobs as she’s jailed for having sex with teen boy, 15, after sending him 25,000 texts
News.content:
AN “OBSESSED” special education teacher sobbed in court as she was jailed for having sex with a 15-year-old student.

Mum-of-two Allison Havemann-Niedrach, 45, was sentenced to 12 years in prison on Friday.



The victim delivered an emotional statement in court describing his months-long relationship with the teacher as “a nightmare”.

The student, who has not been identified, told the court: “For two or three years, I thought it was my fault.”



But the brave pupil added: “I forgive her for what she did.”

Havemann-Niedrach pleaded guilty last April to sexually assaulting the boy when he was in eighth grade over a six month period.

The former Freehold Intermediate School teacher exchanged thousands of messages with the teenager in early 2024.

Within the 25,000 exchanged texts were lurid photo and videos, as well as footage of the pair engaging in sexual conduct, authorities said.

Prosecutors also said the former teacher was “obsessed” with her alleged victim.

She only stopped after she was arrested in June that year, according to cops.



Authorities began probing Havemann-Niedrach when the schools vice principle informed authorities that the teacher had been spotted “rubbing the victim’s back”.

The teacher who spotted her alleged behaviour also claimed they saw Havemann-Niedrach “flirting with him and noticed her touching his leg.”

The victim also allegedly told pals he was dating the married teacher from Ocean County, Jackson.

The boys mum said she became concerned after his sister saw her sitting in his teachers car and saw him texting late at night.

While being quizzed by cops, the boy initially lied, telling them he was dating the teacher’s daughter.



But he eventually admitted he had sex with the predatory suspect.

In court Havemann-Niedrach said: “I apologize profusely for my actions.”

“I am moved by his forgiveness”, she added.

The disgraced teacher is the mother of two small children, and started working at Freehold Intermediate in March 2022.

Before the allegations came to light, Havemann-Niedrach was an active member of the local community.



In 2017 she was one of ten young female leaders awarded by the Girl Scouts of the Jersey Shore as “Phenomenal Women Under 40”, according to Jersey Shore online.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A spokesperson has since cut any ties with the suspect after the allegations arose.

They said: “We want to make it unequivocally clear that Ms. Havemann-Niedrach is no longer associated with Girl Scouts of the Jersey Shore.”

News.title: Do you think Andy Burnham is any different to Keir Starmer?
News.content:
ANDY Burnham might be spades more charismatic and camera-friendly than Sir Keir Starmer – but do you think he is proving to be much different to his wooden predecessor?

Many in the SW1 bubble have spent the last few days looking back — not forward — to ask: What was the point in getting rid of Keir Starmer?



Questions have been raised over the genuine differences between the two Labour figures and of the three biggest crises facing the country — immigration, welfare and defence — there is little in the way of change.

Much of Burnham’s summer cost-of-living package was reheated Starmer stuff – and the PM also appears to have inherited his taste for reviews and consultations instead of action.



Upon the new PM’s coronation, Labour jumped around five percentage points in the polls to leapfrog Reform into pole position. But that bump – and Burnham’s so-called honeymoon period – is already fading.

So, as Mr Burnham arrives back to Parliament following the summer recess – do you think he is any different to calamity Keir?



Have your say in our exclusive poll.

News.title: Four more arrested after boy, 13, stabbed in toilets of Taco Bell after ‘25 youths stormed restaurant with knives’
News.content:
KNIFE ATTACK Four more arrested after boy, 13, stabbed in toilets of Taco Bell after ‘25 youths stormed restaurant with knives’

COPS have made four more arrests after a 13-year-old boy was seriously injured in a stabbing in the toilets of a Taco Bell.

The teenager was attacked at a Taco Bell in Rochdale on Friday evening, August 29, after one diner claimed a group of 25 youths stormed the fast-food restaurant.



He remains in hospital receiving treatment.

Two teenage boys who were previously arrested have been released on bail, while a further four teenage boys have been arrested on suspicion of assault and possession of a bladed article.



Enquiries by the copsare ongoing.

Restrictions under Section 60 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act have been extended in Rochdale town centre until 3pm tomorrow, September 1, 2026.



Detective Superintendent Richard Hunt said: “We continue to make progress on the investigation into this serious attack on a teenage boy in Rochdale.

“Violence on our streets will not be tolerated, and I want to reassure members of the public that we are relentlessly pursuing every lead to bring those responsible to justice.

“We urge anyone who witnessed the incident, was in the town centre at the time, or has any mobile phone, CCTV, or dashcam footage, to come forward and speak to us.”

One man, who was with his wife and children, told Manchester Evening News how a group of “around 20 to 25 youths ran in, some with knives”.



The group then went into the bathroom where he heard ” a load of crying and screaming”.

David Lane claimed: “That’s when the lad got stabbed.

“I grabbed a load of napkins and put pressure on the wound. It looked like he lost a lot of blood. It was a hectic scene.”

Mr Lane said the incident was “horrific” and that his children “shouldn’t have to see that”.

“If it wasn’t for my actions, I think he would have died,” he added.



Anyone with information is urged to contact police on 101 quoting log 2750 of 29/08/2026.

You can also report information via the LiveChat function on GMP’s website: www.gmp.police.uk.

Alternatively, you can contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Disturbing CCTV shows moment mum, 25, dumps newborn baby girl in bin before cleaner discovers body wrapped in bag
News.content:
THIS is the harrowing moment a woman discarded her newborn in a bin after going into labour out of the blue.

CCTV footage shows the 25-year-old carrying a black bag – containing the body of her daughter and placenta – and dumping it.



The incident happened at an estate in Várzea Grande, in the Brazilian state of Mato Grosso, in the early hours of July 23.

A cleaner discovered the remains while sorting rubbish and reported it to the police.



The baby, which still had its umbilical cord attached, was wrapped in the plastic bag.

Post-mortem examinations found she had been born at around 26 weeks of pregnancy, equivalent to roughly six months, and weighed 1lbs 10oz.



Investigators confirmed there were no signs of physical violence, but said that the child had breathed after being born.

This means she was alive for a short period after the delivery.

The exact cause of death is still to be determined, but it is believed that extreme pre-maturity may have contributed.

When officers questioned the mother, she told them she had suspected she was pregnant because of bleeding – but had not received prenatal care or told her husband about it.



She added that she unexpectedly went into labour in the bathroom of her home while he was asleep.

The baby showed no signs of life afterwards.

In a “state of desperation and emotional confusion,” the woman put the child in the bag and threw it away, alongside all the evidence.

She denied taking abortion-inducing substances or receiving help from anyone else.

Abortion is illegal in Brazil, with the exception of a pregnancy resulting from rape, a pregnancy that poses life-threatening risk to the pregnant woman, or if the fetus has a fatal brain defect.



The woman’s husband was also questioned as part of the investigation.

Confirming her account, he told police that he only discovered what had happened days later after the case became public.

Detective Rogério Gomes said the investigation is expected to be completed in the coming days and that the mother is initially expected to be charged with homicide because forensic examinations found the baby had been born alive.

The possible offence could still be changed depending on outstanding forensic reports, with investigators saying an abortion offence could also be considered if evidence shows the birth was deliberately induced.

News.title: Rollercoaster horror as 27 people left trapped 50ft up on Wipeout ride at Pleasurewood Hills theme park in Lowestoft
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

RIDE HELL Rollercoaster horror as 27 people left trapped 50ft up on Wipeout ride at Pleasurewood Hills theme park in Lowestoft

THRILLSEEKERS are stranded 50ft in the air after a rollercoaster broke down and trapped 27 passengers.

Firefighters are currently at Pleasurewood Hills in Lowestoft, Suffolk, after the Wipeout ride ground to a halt.



The carriages are stranded around 15 metres above the ground.

Suffolk Fire and Rescue Service said the trapped passengers are not upside down.



Crews are currently working to safely get all 27 people off the ride.

The dramatic incident unfolded at the popular theme park in Lowestoft, Suffolk.



The Wipeout is a high-speed rollercoaster featuring sharp twists, turns and drops.

It towers more than 130ft high and underwent a £1 million transformation during the end of 2024.

Wipeout is the only remaining Vekoma Boomerang in the UK, which the park says makes it “a truly unique experience”.

Riders are sent forwards through twists, turns, a loop and two cobra rolls, before stopping and reversing along the same track.



Firefighters remain at the scene as efforts to bring the passengers safely back down continue.

The Sun has contacted Pleasurewood Hills for comment.

News.title: ‘Murdered’ woman’s body found in bin bag in park near Premier League ground as manhunt launched over ‘shocking crime’
News.content:
PARK HORROR ‘Murdered’ woman’s body found in bin bag in park near Premier League ground as manhunt launched over ‘shocking crime’

THE body of a woman thought to have been murdered was found in a bin bag in a park close to a Premier League ground, as cops launch a manhunt.

Detectives fear her remains may have been lying there for weeks.

Cops found the woman’s body in the walled garden at Stanley Park, Liverpool, after they were called by a member of the public on Friday at around 5.25pm.



In an update on Monday police said they had not been able to identify the woman as they appealed for more information.



The park is situated between Liverpool’s Anfield Stadium and former Prem ground Goodison Park, now home to Everton‘s women’s team.

The woman has been described as white, aged in her 70s, about 5ft 2in tall, and of small build with strawberry-blonde hair, and was wearing a “distinctive” cerise pink Nike T-shirt when she was found.

Police said a post-mortem examination had taken place but withheld the results “for investigative reasons”.

Detective Superintendent Rachel Wilson appealed for information, saying: “This is a shocking crime.

“If you live in Anfield and have seen or herard any suspiicous, regardless of if you have found it trival or have not reported it, please let us know.

“Pleaes do not assume we hold this information.”

Assistant Chief Constable Andy Ryan said it was possible a visitor to the park may have seen or recorded something which they did not realise was significiant at the time.

News.title: Baby found dead stuffed inside suitcase at Airbnb in Athens as pregnant girl, 15, and Afghan man, 26, quizzed by cops
News.content:
HORROR DISCOVERY Baby found dead stuffed inside suitcase at Airbnb in Athens as pregnant girl, 15, and Afghan man, 26, quizzed by cops

AN URGENT police probe is underway after a baby was found dead inside a suitcase in a Greek Airbnb.

Six people found at the property – including a pregnant 15-year-old girl – were taken to a police station for questioning after the grim discovery in Kypseli, Athens.



Cops were called to the address by the property owner after he alleged that the family had failed to pay rent and were using drugs.

The Airbnb is located in the same neighbourhood where British volunteer Elizabeth Ross, 38, was found stuffed in a suitcase last month.



Inside the property, police found a Greek man, 43, his German wife, 38, and their two sons, aged 12 and nine.

They also discovered a 15-year-old girl and a 26-year-old Afghan man, who said he was the girl’s partner.

The girl and the German woman were both pregnant, police said.

Cops took the Greek dad, the teenage girl and the Afghan man to a police station after officers found small quantities of drugs in their possession.

When police returned to the property to conduct further searches, the German woman and the two boys were getting ready to leave, with their luggage already packed.

During a search of the suitcases, officers found the body of a dead baby inside a container.



The baby had marks on its back, believed to be inflicted by a criminal act, Greek outlet Protothema reports.

Confronted about the shocking find, the woman reportedly told officers the baby was hers and kept the body in the freezer.

But the woman gave conflicting accounts about when the death occurred.

At first she claimed the baby had died two years earlier, but then later said it was eight months ago.

The family had “strange” relationships with one another, the manager of the apartment told the outlet.



He added that cops also discovered sex toys and a camera connected to a computer inside the property.

Sources told Protothema that the nine-year-old boy and 15-year-old girl were suffering from sexually transmitted diseases.

The 12-year-old boy is reportedly in hospital undergoing tests to determine his health.

The family had reportedly stayed at the Airbnb for around a month after making a reservation for two people.

But the manager said: “Then a 9-year-old child came out of a room who did not look like the others at all.



“There was no sequence to the relationships between them, it didn’t make any sense.”

All members of the family are being held at a police station in Athens.

Another property, where the older couple had reportedly been living for two years, was also raided by cops.

Police are probing whether the baby was transferred from the house to the apartment.

The married couple and their daughter are expected to be charged with failure to report the discovery of a dead person.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The 43-year-old man and the Afghan man are also expected to be charged with drug possession.

A coroner’s report is expected to shed light on who the baby’s parents are.

News.title: Mel Stride and Priti Patel replaced in major Tory reshuffle
News.content:
Sir Mel Stride and Dame Priti Patel have left the shadow cabinet as part of a significant reshuffle of the Conservative top team by leader Kemi Badenoch.

Andrew Griffith will replace Sir Mel as shadow chancellor, while Tom Tugendhat will take the place of Dame Priti as shadow foreign secretary.

Badenoch is forming a new shadow cabinet before the party's conference in October.

Claire Coutinho, previously the shadow energy secretary, after her maternity leave will replace Griffith as shadow business secretary and act as his deputy in the ongoing shake-up.

Badenoch paid tribute to Sir Mel's work as shadow chancellor saying he helped the party rebuild economic credibility and become an effective opposition.

A senior Conservative source said: "Kemi is changing the way the Conservative Party approaches economic policy and creating a new economic leadership team for the next phase, focused on growth, higher living standards and fiscal credibility."

Sir Mel, who was appointed to the role following Badenoch's leadership election in 2024, described his time in the senior Tory role as a "great honour".

"I am now looking forward to continuing to make a real contribution to the Conservative team in Parliament and beyond, to build and amplify our vision for Britain, from the back benches."

New shadow chancellor Griffith said the Tories will deliver "an economic revolution" with lower taxes, Britain drilling again to bring energy costs down, slashing red tape and Labour's Employment Rights Act.

"The Conservatives will always back the risk-takers and wealth creators who deliver growth, investment and jobs," he said.

A senior Conservative source described Griffith as a "no-nonsense, pro-growth shadow chancellor with real business experience".

Before he became MP for Arundel and South Downs in 2019, he served as a top executive at Sky and as chairman of Just Eat.

As Treasury minister Griffiths defended Liz Truss' 2022 mini-budget. He also served as City minister responsible for financial services policy.

Liberal Democrat Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said: "Griffith helped deliver the Truss mini-budget that sent mortgages soaring and the economy into turmoil.

"It's clear Conservatives haven't learned a thing. His appointment to shadow chancellor shows they're happy to forfeit any claim to economic credibility in their race to the bottom with Reform UK."

Dame Priti, who had been shadow foreign secretary since 2024, said she will take on a new international role strengthening the Tories relationship with sister parties and centre-right movements abroad.

Badenoch will also need to select a new shadow health secretary after Stuart Andrew confirmed he will be returning to the backbenches.

On Saturday Sir James Cleverly quit the front bench announcing he wants to run for London mayor.

News.title: Messi retires from international football
News.content:
Argentina great Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football, saying it was a decision that "hurt" him but "the time has come".

The 39-year-old, who captained Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar in 2022, has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances, making him the country's all-time leading scorer and most-capped player.

In a statement on Instagram, Messi said he has given everything to the national side but now has "nothing left to give".

He added: "Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply.

"I love, have loved, and will always love being part of the national team.

"I've given it my all, I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some really great young players coming through behind me who deserve their chance."

Earlier in August, Messi said he was considering his future in football after the death of his father, Jorge, who died aged 68 following a a long illness.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner said he wrote his retirement message on 21 July, two days after Argentina lost to Spain in this summer's World Cup final.

Messi, who plays for club side Inter Miami, added: "Today, after what happened with my dad, I'm even more convinced than before."

More to follow.

News.title: The mystery of why so many black Britons still can't swim
News.content:
As I push through the doors, the smell of chlorine hits me. Instantly, I feel sick, and I remember why I don't go swimming. I'm getting ready for my first swimming lesson in over 10 years, trying to convince myself it won't be so bad.

Before I know it, I'm in the water.

I glance around the pool; I'm surrounded by other black women learning to swim, all at different levels. Some are confidently swimming lengths; others, like me, are learning how to feel at home in the water.

I'm learning to breathe properly, dunk my head under and let the water carry me, rather than fight against it. There are so many things to remember.

At the age of 27, I'm still unable to swim - and I'm far from alone.

Swimming ability is not spread evenly across the population; figures compiled by Swim England, swimming's governing body, based on a survey of 4,500 people suggest poorer people, for example, are much less likely to be able to swim, as well as Muslims, people of South Asian descent and children known to social care.

As a black woman, it's the figures for the black community that always jump out to me. Swim England's figures suggest that 67% of black women and 44% of black men in England cannot swim 25 metres unaided - far higher than the national average, and far higher than the numbers for white people (17% of white women and 12% of white men cannot swim 25 metres). Behind those figures, published in 2022, are very different stories.

News.title: Early release scheme could see dangerous criminals released, Conservatives warn
News.content:
On Monday Victims Minister Alex Davies-Jones told the BBC: "We will do nothing that would risk the public or put the public at danger."

Under the early release scheme some 4,500 prisoners are now expected to start being released in tranches from October to ease overcrowding in jails.

The numbers due to be released has been reduced after the government said rapists, those found guilty of serious child sex offences and grooming offences and now those found guilty of manslaughter would be excluded from the scheme.

Given that fewer prisoners will now be released than initially expected this will have a knock-on effect on prison capacity.

Timothy said releasing prisoners serving indefinite sentences under imprisonment for public protection sentences posed its own risk.

Between 2005 and 2012 IPPs were given to some offenders in England and Wales where they were considered to pose a significant risk of causing serious harm to the public. Once they had served a minimum term they could only be released once the Parole Board was satisfied they no longer posed a risk to the public. Although IPPs are no longer imposed many people already serving sentences are stlll in prison.

Timothy told the BBC: "By definition, the people who are still in prison on those sentences are dangerous, because they've all been considered by independent expert assessors who have concluded that they are not safe to release and they would be a danger to the public."

He accepted not enough prisons had been built under the previous Conservative government.

Indefinite prison sentences have previously been handed out in several high-profile cases, including to Tracey Connelly, the mother of Baby P, who was jailed in 2009 after admitting causing or allowing the death of her one-year-old son Peter.

There were 2,271 people serving IPPs, according to Ministry of Justice (MoJ) data up to June this year.

Of those, 856 have never been released because the Parole Board thought it was not safe to do so. Ending indefinite sentences for those still serving them would require new legislation, meaning it could be years before space is freed up.

Davies-Jones told BBC Radio 4's Today programme: "The government's number one priority is to keep the public safe and in order to do that we need a functioning criminal justice system."

She defended the government's decision to look at indefinite sentences as part of ensuring there were enough prison spaces.

"We need to look at every case on its merits individually, and pass the appropriate legislation and we will do that responsibly and we will take our time to get it right," she added.

She said those released would still be monitored.

News.title: This actor was told he had Alzheimer's, now he's performing a one-man show
News.content:
For four days running, Peter Marinker had arrived at rehearsals that were not even taking place. Dementia had muddled the dates in his mind.

Yet he is now preparing to do something most actors would find daunting even with perfect recall: performing a much-loved Samuel Beckett play alone on a London stage.

Marinker, 85, is best known for his voice work: from radio plays and video games to big-budget films like Labyrinth and Paddington in Peru.

On camera he was the adviser to the US president in Love Actually and one of the airline passengers in the drama United 93.

In 2023 he was playing Gandalf in a stage version of Lord of the Rings when he felt himself "switching off" and an understudy had to take over for the rest of the run.

MRI scans and other health checks followed. Then two years ago, he was diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease.

"I just had to accept it," he says. "It explained why I kept losing things and I started laughing at myself, at all the other silly things I do again and again."

News.title: The millennials swapping doom-scrolling for gardening
News.content:
"I was born in '95, so my generation are the kind of ones who know what it's like to grow up with both analogue life and digital culture," said Hannah, from Newport.

She said hobbies such as cooking, sewing and gardening were her generation's "rejection of this hyper-digital world that feels really all-consuming".

She said it was a "tough time for young people" due to the cost of living, climate change, a "dire" jobs market and AI.

"I'm not saying we've had it harder than all other generations," she said.

"But it is challenging being young and maybe having different expectations to those that our parents and grandparents' generations had, and different opportunities."

Hannah said gardening offered a "safe space" to "take control of your little space of land or your balcony or your pots in the kitchen or whatever you're able to have".

It became that for her, she said, when she experienced the loss of her father and grandmother in 2023.

"I didn't use gardening as a conscious means of therapy but I kind of just found myself out here, pottering around," she said.

"It's clichÃ© but kind of creating and nourishing new life and new growth is just really the circle of life."

News.title: The big moves to watch out for before football's transfer window closes
News.content:
The summer transfer window may have been open since 15 June but several Premier League clubs are still scrambling to get key deals over the line before Tuesday's 23:00 BST deadline.

From Julian Alvarez and Enzo Fernandez to Cody Gakpo and Ismaila Sarr, some of football's biggest names could yet be on the move.

But they will have to battle the clock to earn their dream moves before the market closes.

With that in mind, BBC Sport's football reporters have picked out the high-profile moves which could go through during what promises to be a busy ending to the window.

News.title: Jewish community in harder position than immediately after synagogue attack, says rabbi
News.content:
The Jewish community at a synagogue where two men were killed in 2025 feels less safe now than it did immediately after the attack, its rabbi has said almost one year on.

Rabbi Daniel Walker said rising antisemitism, combined with a lack of action to "deal with core problems", had left many members of Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation in Manchester â and British Jews more widely â feeling increasingly vulnerable as the anniversary of the attack approaches.

"I think we're actually almost in a harder position than we were even immediately after the attack," he said ahead of a memorial service for the victims and survivors which will take place later today.

"I think the sense of vulnerability has grown. It hasn't diminished."

News.title: Nursery fined after baby boy burned by bleach
News.content:
Defence advocate Barry Smith KC said the first priority of a nursery was the safety and wellbeing of the children there.

He added: "It is of the utmost regret from all involved - from the director and all staff - that this accident occurred and injury was caused to a young child."

In a statement released via law firm Digby Brown, the family said: "We've had to wait five years for Little Dreams Nursery to admit what happened to our son was their fault but we don't feel the severity of his injuries have been acknowledged.

"We trusted them to take care of him and for such an injury to happen to a 10-month-old baby is indefensible.

"In the months and years that followed, we had to watch our boy deal with the consequences of something that was never his fault. No parent should have to experience that, but we are thankful what happened hasn't had a more serious or longer-lasting impact."

The statement concluded: "Today we close the most horrific chapter of our lives and we want to thank everyone who has supported us during this time and now request our privacy as we move forward."

Little Dreams said the safety, wellbeing and care of every child entrusted to them was of the "highest priority".

"We deeply regret that this incident was able to occur and are profoundly sorry for the distress and impact it has had on the child and their family," the nursery said.

News.title: Emergency measures needed to stop teachers quitting, say Lib Dems
News.content:
Burnt out teachers urgently need better working hours and more support to stop them leaving the profession, the Liberal Democrats say, as the new term approaches.

Nearly half of the teachers surveyed by the party in England said they were planning to quit the classroom in the next five years, with many saying they felt overworked and stressed.

The Lib Dems are urging new Education Secretary Lucy Powell to fully fund teachers' pay, rather than raiding school budgets to cover increases, and to bring in limits on overtime.

The Department for Education said last year saw the lowest rate of teachers leaving the profession since 2010 but acknowledged there was "more to do".

The survey asked more than 900 teachers, headteachers and Special Educational Needs Coordinators (SENCOs) across England how long they planned to stay in teaching.

Almost half of those in post said they were considering leaving teaching in the next five years, while one in ten were planning to spend less than a year in the job.

More than three quarters of those surveyed, which included former teachers, said they had felt "frequently or constantly burnt out" while at work.

Respondents cited high workloads on marking, lesson preparation and other tasks, which they said gave them less time in the classroom.

The Liberal Democrats' schools spokesperson Caroline Voaden said this pointed to a government that is "not listening" to the profession.

"We rely on teachers to educate our children, the least we can do is make sure they want to come back after the summer," she said.

Teacher retention is a challenge successive governments have had to grapple with.

The National Education Union (NEU) reported that 4 in 10 teachers were planning to quit over "huge workloads and excessive accountability" in 2019.

This latest survey was also conducted with the help of the NEU, as well as the Association of School and College Leaders (ASCL).

"After over a decade of austerity and chronic underfunding in our schools the system is on its knees" said the NEU's general secretary Daniel Kebede.

"The new academic year is the perfect time for Andy Burnham to signal a fresh start for our schools" he added.

"That means fully funding the pay award and properly funding all our schools and colleges to stem the recruitment and retention crisis and give children the education they deserve."

"As Lucy Powell enters her first term as education secretary the Liberal Democrats are calling for her first act to be to introduce an emergency package of 'back to school' measures to face this crisis head on," Voaden said.

The Lib Dem proposals include the government fully funding teacher's pay, which will increase in England by 3.5% from September, with an additional 3% the year after.

Currently, half of the pay increase will come from existing school budgets.

The party is also calling for proper enforcement of teacher's legally mandated working hours, the introduction of reasonable limits on overtime, and for all schools to be required to introduce flexible working policies.

The party did not identify where funding might come from to pay for the policies.

An education department spokesperson said: "We know teachers do an incredible job and we're determined to make sure that dedication is matched with the right support.

"Last year saw one of the lowest rates of teachers leaving the profession since 2010, and a record number of teachers returning to the classroom, but we know there's more to do.

"We're taking action by announcing pay awards of almost 17% over two years, funding schools to improve maternity pay and offering targeted support to normalise flexible working and manageable workloads so that more teachers stay in our classrooms and thrive."

News.title: Business groups urge Swinney to scrap 'ineffective' food price cap plan
News.content:
The SRC said the policy also risked forcing small shops which are not covered by the proposed legislation to be uncompetitive.

"Scottish consumers benefit from the most affordable food prices in western Europe," MacDonald-Russell added.

"We know food price inflation is a problem, but the best model to deal with it is the one we have right now and price caps are going to make that worse.

"It is giving a false promise that it is going to be able to help with something.

"In reality, there is as good a chance it is going to make the overall cost of a shopping basket higher, because the cost of the scheme as well as the cap have to be absorbed by businesses."

It is thought the proposals would require changes to the UK Internal Markets Act of 2020, which was brought in after Brexit to prevent trade barriers and regulatory divergence between England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland as powers returned from the EU.

The Scottish government said helping people with the cost of living was a "top priority".

A spokesperson added: "Ministers have welcomed engagement with stakeholders, including retailers, food producers and farmers on proposals for food price controls.

"A consultation will launch shortly for further views."

News.title: Parents of seriously ill children should get paid leave, says commissioner
News.content:
Parents of children with serious illnesses or disabilities should be entitled to paid leave from work, the children's commissioner Dame Rachel de Souza has said.

She called on the government to introduce a legal right to 12 weeks of paid leave at 90% of normal pay in order to lift the "immense pressure" and lost earnings families face when a child develops a debilitating condition.

Her intervention came as the government continued to consult on how to financially support families and unpaid carers looking after ill children in England, Scotland and Wales.

She said: "Parents should not be forced to choose between being at their seriously ill child's bedside and keeping their job."

Dame Rachel said that parents have told her of the "impossible choices" they have made when "splitting time between caring for their seriously ill and disabled children and trying to hold down a job".

She has also backed a "right to return to work" following extended periods of leave, saying it could help "families whose children have complex or fluctuating needs to remain in employment while providing the care their children need".

Dame Rachel called unpaid carer's leave to be increased from five to 10 days a year, and for the introduction of a form of paid carer's leave.

It comes after campaigning by the parents of Hugh Menai-Davis, who died of cancer aged six in 2021.

His parents Frances and Ceri Menai-Davis have advocated for a change to employment law that would require employers to guarantee three months' salaries to parents whose child faces serious physical or mental illness.

"There's no specific right that allows the parents to legally be by the bedside of the child in hospital," Ceri Menai-Davis said in June.

"If you're a parent with a child, there is nowhere else you are going to be other than their bedside."

A consultation on reforms to the support available to families and carers is due to close on Monday.

Kate Dearden, minister for the future of work, said: "Serious childhood illness is a heartbreaking situation for families.

"I've been incredibly moved by the powerful stories we have heard, and we will move quickly to consider how we can strengthen support and employment rights for families facing serious childhood illness."

News.title: Hints of fiery finale for last ever episode of River City
News.content:
Johnny McKnight has written for River City for almost a decade so, when it was announced that the show was drawing to a close after 24 years, he asked if he could write the final episode.

"Those moments don't come up very often with long-running shows so I thought it might be cathartic and a nice way to say goodbye as a writer," he says.

Details of the episode, which will air on Monday, are a closely-guarded secret but images released showing a bloodied Lenny Murdoch amidst a dramatic fire scene suggest the show's arch-villain, played by Frank Gallagher, is at the centre of it.

McKnight says he felt a huge responsibility to the show's fans to give them a satisfying ending.

He points to cult TV shows whose endings have divided fans - like The Sopranos, Dexter, Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Angel.

McKnight says: "I'm just part of a massive collective team effort and I hope we've done the fans proud to the end."

He thinks the show has always managed to walk a fine line between comedy and drama.

"River City is what I think it is to be Scottish. Our punches have punchlines.

"We take our trauma and we find a way to tell it in a pub that makes it palatable, and the humour co-exists alongside the drama."

News.title: UK raises case of British activist detained by settlers in West Bank with Israel
News.content:
The UK Foreign Office says it has raised the detention of a British national in the occupied West Bank with Israeli authorities.

Finn Joughin, a 22-year-old student activist, was arrested in Umm Al-Kheir on Saturday after he was forcibly detained by Israeli settlers who had advanced on the Palestinian village.

There has been a surge in attacks by settlers on Palestinians and their property in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war, which was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023.

All settlements are illegal under international law. Outposts are also illegal under Israeli law, although they are often supported by state services and funding.

The confrontation on Saturday took place in a town near Hebron that has been recently surrounded by settlers.

According to other activists who witnessed what happened, Palestinian children were playing football when children from settler families started intervening. They then ran to a house and started to dismantle a fence.

Footage posted online by both settlers and activists and seen by the BBC appears to show Joughin standing by the fence and trying to protect it using his body as a child pushes against him.

Settlers removed Joughin forcefully and took the London-based student to an outpost.

Israeli police said a foreign national "who disrupted public order" was detained by security personnel of a settler community who suspected him of an indecent act against a minor and other offences.

In a statement on Sunday, police said the suspect was transferred to their custody for questioning before documents relating to the case were sent to the Population and Immigration Authority for review.

"This was carried out as part of ongoing cooperation and efforts to prevent provocative activity involving confrontations and disturbances," police said.

A lawyer for Joughin said: "We absolutely deny all the allegations."

Inbar Shaked Vardi told the BBC that the student was initially accused of assault.

But Shaked Vardi said police later added to the paperwork an allegation of an indecent act.

Joughin is being deported back to the UK on a flight scheduled for Monday afternoon, according to his lawyer.

"So far they have not decided officially on closing the case," Shaked Vardi said.

Joughin is the only one being investigated and as he is being deported, "it's safe to assume they won't continue to pursue charges against him", she said.

"Police use deportation in order to get what they want â which is to get activists outside of the West Bank while continuing to allow settlers to do what they do", she added.

Activists who were with Joughin at the time deny there was any inappropriate behaviour.

"In every single instance, it was the settler kids who approached Finn," fellow activist Matthew, who declined to give his surname, told the BBC.

News.title: Fears over 'high risk' crossing after train crash death
News.content:
An investigation is continuing into how a delivery vehicle and a train collided on a crossing, killing a van driver.

The incident happened off Martin Lane and Whitehouse Lane in Burscough, West Lancashire, on Saturday at about 15:00 GMT, when a train from Southport to Manchester collided with what is understood to be a supermarket delivery vehicle.

People living in the area have told the BBC that it was not uncommon for the gate on the crossing to be left open at times by people using it.

The claims have been put to Network Rail, which, while not able to comment on the claims, said it was involved in an investigation alongside British Transport Police and the Rail Accident Investigation Board.

The train was travelling towards Burscough town centre when the collision happened. A woman who was on board the train described seeing the van travelling along Martin Lane before it collided with the Northern train.

The crossing where the crash took place is not a full level crossing, but one operated by people as and when they use it.

It has lights and makes warning noises when the gate is not shut.

The Met Gala has taken the unprecedented step of canceling its theme for 2027 after the withdrawal of its honoree, the influential fashion designer John Galliano.

Earlier this month, the Metropolitan Museum of Art announced that the Costume Institute's spring exhibition next year would be titled “John Galliano: Horizon,” recognizing the work of the British designer, who is widely considered to be one of the most powerful — and polarizing — tastemakers of the past four decades. The nine-month exhibit would have begun with the accompanying red carpet gala, one of the biggest nights on the fashion calendar.

The move proved instantly controversial since Galliano was temporarily exiled from the industry after being convicted of an antisemitic hate crime by a French court in 2011.

In a statement released Monday, Galliano announced he had withdrawn from being honored.

“After much reflection and discussion with The Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time,” he said.

open image in gallery Met Gala chair Anna Wintour has championed fashion designer John Galliano since the beginning of his career ( Getty Images )

“I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it.

“I do not want the debate surrounding me to place the Met in a difficult position or distract from the remarkable work of the Costume Institute,” he wrote. “I also recognize and respect that an exhibition honoring my work would be painful for some.”

His decision came after a number of the Met’s donors had expressed their opposition to the theme and accompanying exhibition.

The New York Times reports that Galliano’s departure came hours before key members of the Met’s board of trustees were scheduled to discuss the fate of the exhibit in the wake of more backlash.

Julie Menin, the speaker of the City Council, sent a letter to Met leadership last week, becoming the first local politician to oppose the planned Galliano exhibition.

The Democrat called the since-canceled show “a gut punch to the Jewish community in our city, who are already reeling” in an interview published over the weekend.

open image in gallery John Galliano (pictured in a Dior store in Shanghai in 2010) was briefly exiled from the fashion world after his 2011 antisemitic comments surfaced ( AFP/Getty )

The event would have celebrated Galliano’s work, with many celebrities expected to wear his archival designs or interpretations of his most famous looks.

Galliano would have been only the third living designer to be the subject of the exhibit, following Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo of Comme des Garçons in 2017.

Galliano became a polarizing figure in the fashion world in 2011 when his racist comments surfaced, including a video taken at a Paris restaurant in which he used antisemitic insults at other customers.

The designer was convicted of committing public insults based on race and religion from two incidents in Paris and faced a fine equivalent to $8,500. He subsequently lost his prestigious position as creative director at Dior after a 14-year tenure.

During his trial, Galliano testified that he didn’t remember one of his outbursts at a Paris cafe due to a triple addiction to sleeping pills, Valium and alcohol.

“I have an addiction. I am currently seeking treatment,” he told the courtroom at the time.

The designer, now 65, began his career at Givenchy in 1995 before becoming Dior’s creative director in 1997, a role he held until 2011 and during which he became known for his romantic, anti-minimalist designs. His looks became some of the most sought-after on the red carpet, and he designed Princess Diana’s Met Gala dress, a lace-trimmed Dior slip that she wore to the event in 1996.

In 2014, three years after his antisemitic comments surfaced, he was made the creative director of the Parisian fashion house Maison Margiela. He remained in that post until 2024.

Today, his designs are still present on virtually every red carpet. Stevie Nicks wore a custom look designed by Galliano for Zara at the 2026 Met Gala. For the 2024 event, Zendaya wore a custom Galliano for Margiela look, which was inspired by his 1996 Dior collection.

A 2024 documentary by Kevin Macdonald explored the designer’s redemption as he spent time in rehabilitation for alcohol addiction and met prominent Jewish leaders to seek forgiveness.

Speaking about the footage and two attacks during the documentary, Galliano, who was born in the British territory of Gibraltar, said: “It was a disgusting thing, foul thing that I did. It was just horrific.”

open image in gallery John Galliano, pictured here onstage on the Dior runway in January 2010, lost his position at the fashion house after his antisemitic comments surfaced ( Getty Images )

open image in gallery Stevie Nicks attended this year’s Met Gala in a custom look designed by John Galliano for Zara ( Getty )

Reflecting on the events, the designer added: “I can say I’m not racist, but every day you actually learn that all of us are a bit. But we just need to unlearn it and like immigrants. I am one. I was one.”

The Guardian reported that a Met exhibition was originally planned for 2024 but was postponed after some board members voiced concerns.

Wintour had previously said in a release that the exhibit would not shy away from “any of the darkness in John’s past” and that it would take into account the “full arc” of his career.

Wintour said in a statement released Monday: “John’s decision that the exhibition devoted to his work should not take place at this time is very courageous and a measure of the man he is. I believe this is the right decision, and both he and the Museum have my full support.”

Andrew Bolton, Curator in Charge of The Met's Costume Institute, said he recognized the “pain and concern this exhibition has caused.”

“After extensive discussion, I support the decision not to proceed. I remain deeply grateful to my colleagues and to the advisors, lenders, collaborators, and community leaders who contributed their knowledge, trust, and perspectives to the project.”

Visitors to a beach made famous by the BBC series Poldark have been urged to stay well away from a cliff fall which has destroyed a beachside cave in Cornwall.

Holywell Cave was an ancient and cherished natural landmark at Holywell Bay near Newquay where locals and tourists visited the hollow for many years.

A major cliff fall, which happened over the bank holiday weekend, has caused tonnes of stone to collapse and cover the cave entrance.

The cave, also known as St Cuthbert's Cave, had been tucked under the southern cliffs of Kelsey Head.

The sight of the cliff fall over a beloved cave has sparked sadness from many residents and tourists. Chris Barnard, who lives near Callington, Cornwall, told the BBC: "I was shocked when I first saw the photographs because it's such an iconic location and such a popular location.

"The fact it's gone is not nice... it's gone forever.

"The collapse must have happened overnight because, if people were inside, it could have been a catastrophe."

open image in gallery Residents and tourists have been urged to stay away from the cliff fall at Holywell Cave on Holywell Bay ( Holywell Bay Surf Life Saving Club )

Another person wrote: “This is so sad, an important part of Cornish history wiped out.”

Holywell was used in Poldark, which was seen to be owned by Ross’s rivals, the Warleggans. It features in Series 4 and 5 of the BBC drama, most notably as the spot where Drake Carne secretly meets Morwenna, and in dramatic scenes involving Ross Poldark.

The famous twin offshore islands of Carter’s and Gulls Rocks provide a dramatic backdrop to the show’s action.

The National Trust, which is the guardian of the cave, said: "We are aware of the substantial cliff fall at Holywell Bay and are monitoring the situation closely.

“Our priority is the safety of visitors and we urge people to stay well back from the affected area, both on the beach and from clifftop paths, as the cliff remains unstable and further rock falls are possible.

"We know Holywell Cave is a much-loved feature of this coastline and many people will be saddened by what has happened. At present the cave is completely covered by the rock fall and is inaccessible."

open image in gallery Inside Holywell Cave before the cliff fall ( Holywell Bay Surf Life Saving Club )

Newquay Coastguard said: "Sadly overnight a substantial rock fall has sealed off the cave to Holy Well on Holywell Beach.

"This area is still unstable and we advise that you to stay clear of this rockfall.

"Heavy rain after a prolonged dry spell may lead to further incidents along the coast path. Keep clear of the edge whilst walking along the top of cliffs and stay clear of the bottom.

"If you see someone in difficulty along the coast, dial 999 and ask for the coastguard."

Lionel Messi has retired from international football, bringing the curtain down on his Argentina career after falling short in the World Cup final in July.

Perhaps the greatest player of all time, Messi had been hoping to lead his side to back-to-back tournament triumphs but suffered a 1-0 defeat to Spain in extra time.

The 39-year-old made 207 appearances for his country, the second most by any men’s international footballer, scoring 125 times across a career that spanned more than two decades.

open image in gallery Lionel Messi celebrates with team-mates after Argentina's 3-2 victory over Egypt at World Cup 2026 ( Getty Images )

Messi revealed he decided to retire two days after Argentina’s defeat to Spain in the World Cup final on 19 July, but then delayed announcing his decision.

Messi’s father, Jorge Messi, then passed away in August at the age of 68 after a long illness, after his son had returned to the pitch following the World Cup with his club Inter Miami.

“After the time that has passed since the final, and after giving it a lot of thought, I want to let everyone know that I am retiring from the national team,” Messi wrote on Instagram.

“It was a decision that hurt—and still hurts deep down—but I understand that the time has come,” he said.

Recommended The impossible Lionel Messi question Argentina must answer at the end of a golden era

Messi’s crowning moment with Argentina came in 2022 when he captained his country to their third World Cup following a dramatic victory over France in Qatar.

Having made his senior debut for Argentina in 2005 at the age of 18, Messi also led Argentina to the 2014 World Cup final where they lost to Germany in extra time in Brazil.

Messi previously retired from Argentina in 2016, aged 29, after he suffered a fourth consecutive major final loss with his country following defeat to Chile in the Copa America final.

Messi returned, however, and finally won a major senior title with Argentina at the 2021 Copa America, which was followed by the World Cup and then another Copa America in 2024.

open image in gallery Messi ended his long quest to win the World Cup in 2022 ( Getty Images )

The forward finishes his career as the second leading World Cup goalscorer behind Kylian Mbappe after the pair each surpassed Miroslav Klose’s record tally during the tournament.

An eight-time Ballon d’Or winner and Barcelona icon, Messi has continued playing for Inter Miami in Major League Soccer, scoring four goals in a 7-1 win over Montreal on Saturday.

But Messi said he “did not know how to carry on” following the death of his father Jorge. Messi also said that Argentina’s defeat to Spain brought “immense pain”.

Lionel Messi’s statement on international retirement in full

“After the time that has passed since the final, and after giving it a lot of thought, I want to let everyone know that I am retiring from the national team...

“It was a decision that hurt—and still hurts deep down—but I understand that the time has come. I swear to you that I always gave it my all—not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too; I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you feel proud to be Argentine through football.

“Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply. I love, have loved, and will always love being part of the national team. I’ve given everything I had; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some great young players coming up who deserve to be here.

“Thank you for all the affection over these past 20 years. I will miss hearing you from the pitch so much. Now I’ll be just one of you, cheering and supporting from the outside (through the good times and the bad—especially the bad).

“Thank you to my family for always being there, for accompanying me on this journey—so beautiful, yet so difficult. Thank you to every coach, team-mate, and official I’ve shared this path with. I take with me unforgettable memories and moments.

“I leave with the peace of mind and pride of having given you—alongside my team-mates—moments we once only dreamed of. It was an incredible experience to live this with you all. I love you! Thank you, God, for making me Argentine. Let's go, Argentina!

“PS - I wrote these words on July 21st, two days after the final. Today, after what happened with my dad, I am even more convinced than before.”

Prediction platform Kalshi has handed former U.S. congressman George Santos a lifetime ban and fined him $71,356 over allegations of insider trading.

According to a disciplinary filing released by the firm, its compliance team determined there was reasonable cause to conclude that the former lawmaker participated in unlawful trades.

The decision comes amid a surge in questionable transactions across prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket, creating fresh oversight hurdles as law enforcement and regulators step up their focus on the expanding industry.

In June, Kalshi referred Santos to the U.S. Department of Justice following the discovery of unusual account activity.

Santos was ousted from Congress following charges of identity theft and fraud ( AFP via Getty Images )

Fresh out of prison for wire fraud and identity theft, Santos allegedly began a new scheme by fixing the odds on a bet of whether he would attend President Donald Trump’s State of the Union address in February, unnamed sources told NPR at the time.

He posted on X a day before Trump’s speech saying that he would be at the U.S. Capitol for it. But the next day, he said he would instead be watching the speech from an airport TV, writing on X that it was “not part of the plan!”

Before his announcement, Santos had allegedly placed bets on Kalshi that he was not going to attend the State of the Union, NPR reported.

Several social media users immediately accused him of running another scheme.

Recommended George Santos settles federal probe over State of the Union bets on Kalshi

Santos agreed to a $35,000 settlement with federal investigators to resolve the DOJ inquiry. In a statement at the time, Santos’ lawyer said his client had a “genuine intention” to attend the State of the Union, even booking a hotel and plane ticket before a winter storm scuttled the plans.

“Mr. Santos concealed neither his intention to attend, nor his change of plans to not attend the SOTU, from anyone," attorney Joseph Murray said. “There was absolutely no intent to deceive any person, nor intent to manipulate any market."

Santos addressed complaints about the SOTU bets on his podcast in March, saying, “I guess people lost money. Some people made unexpected money. That’s to show you how fragile these markets are.”

Santos was ousted from Congress following charges of identity theft and fraud. He pleaded guilty to fraud and identity theft in 2024 and a federal judge in New York sentenced him to 87 months in prison. The judge said the former congressman showed no remorse for campaign donors and voters he lied to and swindled out of money.

U.S. President Donald Trump commuted his prison sentence in October, after the 37-year-old former Republican congressman served just 84 days.

“George Santos was somewhat of a ‘rogue,’ but there are many rogues throughout our Country that aren’t forced to serve seven years in prison,” Trump wrote on Truth Social.

He went on to praise Santos for having “the Courage, Conviction, and Intelligence to ALWAYS VOTE REPUBLICAN!”
