Tory leader Kemi Badenoch has ruthlessly sacked her shadow chancellor Sir Mel Stride and replaced him with one of the architects of Liz Truss’s disastrous mini-Budget

New shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith was financial secretary to the Treasury – number three in the department – when Ms Truss’s mini-Budget caused a run on the gilt market and almost bankrupted the country.

He was a strong advocate of the former prime minister’s plans to slash taxes and his appointment appears to be an indication that Ms Badenoch wants the party to take a more aggressive direction after the cautious approach of Sir Mel.

The Tory leader has consistently refused to apologise for the Truss mini-Budget or throw the former PM out of the party.

Now she has put one of her key lieutenants and supporter of the hardcore tax-cutting approach in charge of economic policy as she tries to take on Nigel Farage and Reform.

open image in gallery Mel Stride is out of the shadow cabinet ( PA )

In a hint that he still supports the Truss approach to the country’s finances, Mr Griffiths pointedly tweeted: “The Conservatives will always back the risk-takers and wealth creators who deliver growth, investment and jobs.”

He tweeted: “It is a huge honour to become shadow chancellor for the party I joined as a teenager under Margaret Thatcher. Working as a team, we Conservatives will deliver an economic revolution.

“We will deliver lower, simpler taxes, get Britain drilling again to bring down energy costs, slash the red tape holding Britain back, and scrap the job-killing measures in Labour’s (Un)Employment Rights Act.”

Chief Treasury secretary Emma Reynolds said: “The new shadow chancellor backed Liz Truss to be PM and he was a Treasury minister during the Tories disastrous 2022 mini budget which left families paying the price. Same old Tories, same old economic policies.”

Lib Dem deputy leader and Treasury spokesperson Daisy Cooper said: “Griffith helped deliver the Truss mini-budget that sent mortgages soaring &the economy into turmoil.

It’s clear Conservatives haven't learned a thing. His appointment to shadow chancellor shows they're happy to forfeit any claim to economic credibility in their race to the bottom with Reform UK.”

Labour former Treasury minister Torsten Bell noted: “The best the Conservatives have to offer on the economy is Liz Truss’s biggest cheer leader. No learning curve at all.”

The move comes as the Conservative leader embarks on her first major reshuffle of her top team amid concerns it has been underperforming and holding the party’s recovery back.

A reshuffle had been inevitable after Sir James Cleverly resigned as shadow housing secretary to run as London mayor and with Julia Lopez shadowing the former science ministry, which has been abolished by Andy Burnham.

The decision to ditch Sir Mel, a former welfare secretary who had been a major critic of Truss’s mini-Budget, comes after she sacked Dame Priti Patel as shadow foreign secretary and replaced her with former security minister Tom Tugendhat.

Shadow health secretary Stuart Andrew has also been shown the exit door after the party made little impression in taking on Labour over its handling of the NHS.

However, after the steady hand of Sir Mel on Treasury policy, Ms Badenoch had been urged within the party to go for a bolder strategy with a new face.

This has been confirmed with the appointment of Mr Griffith, a former Sky News executive.

A senior Conservative source said: “Kemi is changing the way the Conservative Party approaches economic policy and creating a new economic leadership team for the next phase, focused on growth, higher living standards and fiscal credibility.

“The team will be led by Andrew Griffith, a no-nonsense, pro-growth shadow chancellor with real business experience.”

Claire Coutinho, who is due to go on maternity leave, will be Mr Griffith's deputy across the economic brief, as well as shadow business secretary.

open image in gallery Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch, and Andrew Griffith, the new shadow chancellor ( PA )

When she returns her task will be to make sure growth translates into higher living standards. Richard Fuller will be focused on fiscal discipline and the savings work which underpins the economic programme.

Ms Coutinho had impressed as shadow energy secretary and was credited in pushing Mr Burnham to look at abandoning some of former energy secretary Ed Miliband’s hard line net zero policies on blocking new drilling for oil and gas in the North Sea.

She is likely to be replaced by Scottish MP Andrew Bowie as shadow energy secretary with rising star Harriet Cross expected to become shadow Scottish secretary.

According to the senior party source, the new Conservative Economic Unit will be the driving force of the shadow cabinet’s business and economic policies.

Sir Mel had started the party on its road to recovery and overseen introducing the policy of scrapping stamp duty. But he had generally urged caution, especially on reversing Labour controversial National Insurance hike which has caused the jobs market to dry up.

In a statement, Sir Mel said: “The Conservative party must continue to champion an approach which is both radical and deliverable. It is essential that the next Conservative government does things very differently, backing business like never before and getting government out of the way. The Conservatives have a good story to tell on this now and one that I know will continue to grow stronger and stronger under Kemi’s leadership.”

Ms Badenoch paid tribute to Sir Mel and Dame Priti in a statement

She said: “Like Priti, Mel came into the job at an exceptionally difficult point for the Conservative Party. He brought experience, seriousness and stability when those things were badly needed.

“He helped us steady the ship, rebuild economic credibility and become an effective opposition, and I am genuinely grateful for his contribution. The Conservative Party would not have got where we are without his work and his very effective skewering of Rachel Reeves and her disastrous time as chancellor.

“Mel has been very supportive of the new economic team and the party, and been exceptionally loyal, and I will always be grateful to him for the work he has done.”

News.title: Lionel Messi retires from international football
News.content:
Argentina captain Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football in a statement on Instagram.

The Inter Miami forward led his national team to victory in the 2022 World Cup, and his last game for his country was the 1-0 defeat by Spain in last month’s final.

Messi, who turned 39 in June and became arguably the greatest player of all time during his time at Barcelona, has retired having scored 125 goals in 207 internationals.

“After the time that has passed since the final, and after giving it a lot of thought, I want to let everyone know that I am retiring from the national team,” wrote Messi, whose father, Jorge, died on August 8.

News.title: Manchester United’s attack may be their best form of defence this season
News.content:
Is attack going to be Manchester United’s best form of defence this season?

There was plenty to like going forward, particularly once United had nudged their way in front after their second lucky break of what had hitherto looked like being a tricky afternoon.

Give this team a little space and they have the attacking players to inflict some serious damage, none more so than Bruno Fernandes who, just five days after collecting the PFA Players’ Player of the Year award, scored a hat-trick in what was another inspired performance.

Ipswich Town will testify to that after a sobering second half when it felt like United were going to score with every raid forward and, for a time, even threaten to equal the nine goals they scored against the promoted side at this ground 31 years ago.

In the returning Marcus Rashford, whom manager Michael Carrick likened to a “new signing”, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo and, of course, Fernandes, United have an intriguing blend of attacking players. Throw in Kobbie Mainoo who, on another day, would have stolen the headlines with an imperious display in central midfield, and one thing United are not lacking for is creativity.

News.title: Robinson’s Victorian-style bowling figures secure series victory over Pakistan
News.content:
The only missing aspect was a five-fer which would have brought a 100th Test wicket. Even so, his career average is now 19.53, the best for England since Frank Tyson of those with 50 or more wickets.

Mr Nude Nuts, as Matthew Hayden called him, could be devastating against Australia and, like Root the captain, deserves to be judged on what happens in his second incarnation rather than what went before.

Robinson’s pace has lingered around the 79mph mark and inevitably that throws up Rob Key’s assertion you cannot succeed in Test cricket bowling in the 70s with the keeper standing up. Key was referring to county bowlers pitching it up and relying on the Dukes ball to do the rest.

It was thrown in his face in Australia but Michael Neser and Scott Boland are not county trundlers: they extract more energy off the pitch than that.

Robinson is also no dobber. His high release point combined with a mastery of length means he is always threatening the top of off stump. He also knows which way the ball is going to nip, giving no clues to the batsmen due to his sleight of hand skills.

With Jamie Smith improving under the tutelage of Sarah Taylor, he can operate with the keeper standing up which pins batsmen in the crease, bringing all modes of dismissals into play. Robinson was as effective with the new ball as the old: his two seven-over spells were two for 13 and two for 11.

How snarling Robinson adds edge and precision

At 32, he has become a combination of Stuart Broad and James Anderson, although down on their pace with the height and bounce of the former, and tricks of the latter. He can move the new ball further either way than Anderson or Broad but the question is whether he has their durability and sheer competitiveness.

He has not been tested this summer by pitches or opponents. He has not bowled more than 18 overs in an innings and was injured when England played on the best batting pitch at the Oval. He was not trusted at Trent Bridge because the old management had burned their fingers before. That decision may well have cost the coach his job.

Like Broad and Anderson he has a snarl too, sending Abdullah Shafique on his way with a word or two. There was no need for that but maybe it was just a carried away reaction to bowling an absolute beauty that angled in, seamed away and hit the top of off.

News.title: Chelsea are great entertainers but possess clear weakness
News.content:
Xabi Alonso takes charge of his first home Premier League game in charge of Chelsea as they host Brighton at Stamford Bridge. Both sides were in action in two different competitions on Thursday night. Chelsea reached the League Cup third round as they beat Luton 2-0 at Stamford Bridge, with former Brighton man Danny Welbeck scoring on his debut. Brighton meanwhile confirmed their place in the Conference League group stages with a 4-0 aggregate win over Tromso.

Chelsea began their Premier League campaign last Monday in a west London derby against Fulham at Craven Cottage, winning 3-2 in Alonso’s first game as Chelsea boss. Enzo Fernandez was not involved in Chelsea’s squad against Luton on Thursday and has been heavily linked with a move to Manchester City. Alonso was asked about Enzo’s absence on Thursday and did not confirm whether the Argentine would be involved today.

“It was just because of the game today [on Thursday] and we have other players who need minutes,” Alonso said. “[On Wednesday], in the afternoon. It is a decision that I took. Enzo is a good professional. He is training well and I have nothing to say about this. It was just decisions that we have to take thinking about the game that we were playing tonight [Thursday]. We will see for Sunday [today].”

Brighton began their Premier League campaign in emphatic style as they thrashed Aston Villa 4-0 at home seven days ago. Jack Hinshelwood scored twice in that game but will now miss a number of weeks with an ankle injury. They are also without Yankuba Minteh, who has been linked with a move to Liverpool this summer but is unavailable due to injury.

“When the window is closed I demand from him [Minteh] that he is fully committed to this club,” Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler said. “There are dreams and wishes for players, but in the end we always need to figure out what is best for the club.

“We have had an exchange with him. At the moment he is definitely a Brighton player. It is very important to understand his thoughts but also our planning. As a club we try to develop players. The last few years have shown that the whole environment gave him a lot of trust and belief that he is capable of having this progress. It is always a give and take and he has gotten a lot from us.”

Brighton won both Premier League meetings last season, winning 3-1 in this fixture last September. Brighton have won five of their last eight top-flight meetings with Chelsea. Team news from Stamford Bridge to follow shortly.

News.title: Moses Itauma lifted out of ring after losing IBF title bout to Filip Hrgovic
News.content:
Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of the heavyweight clash between Moses Itauma and Filip Hrgovic.

Itauma is on the cusp of becoming a British boxing star, but for now there remain questions. It is not that people doubt his talents, more that he needs to prove them emphatically to the wider boxing world.

At just 21, Itauma has been creating rumblings since 2023. He has 10 straight knockouts. He is undefeated. His last two wins were against Dillian Whyte and Jermaine Franklin, but he is yet to beat a fighter you might regard as a gatekeeper to a title fight.

Hrgovic might normally be seen as that gatekeeper. At 34, the Croatian has plenty of experience in the ring, with 21 fights bringing 20 wins, 15 of them by knockout. His only loss was against Daniel Dubois in 2024, but his wins since then have been against Joe Joyce, David Adeleye and Dave Allen. Not the highest quality, by any means. Hrgovic, then, has something to prove to us too.

However, this is no eliminator, this is for the full IBF world heavyweight championship. A win for Itauma would see him become the second-youngest world heavyweight champion in boxing history.

As Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury circle one another, threatening to never fight at all, Itauma looks set to be Britain’s next heavyweight star. All he has to do is win at the O2 Arena tonight. If he does that, he could then be a fixture at the top of the sport for a decade, perhaps more.

Ringwalks are expected at around 10.30pm for the main event. So if men in dressing gowns is your thing, get ready.

News.title: £380m = zero points: Big-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle
News.content:
“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the new signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five new arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

News.title: Lawrence seizes his opportunity on rain-ruined day at Lord’s
News.content:
On a bleak day for batting, Dan Lawrence seized an opportunity that he must have feared had passed him by.

Lawrence was one of the victims of Bazball excess, shoved up to open in place of Zak Crawley two years ago in a punt that backfired and could have ended his Test career.

It took the sudden retirement of Ben Stokes and an injury to first-choice replacement Sam Curran to open up a position at No 6, Lawrence’s natural home, and it has come at just the right time.

At 29 he is a much more rounded cricketer than the one who debuted in Sri Lanka under Joe Root in 2021 and he showed it here with a hard-fought half-century on a gloomy, dank Saturday when only 25 overs were possible between the frequent drizzly showers, forcing MCC into a 50 per cent ticket refund.

It was a second fifty in three innings since his recall and he will not have faced many tougher conditions than this, with the ball seaming around on a spiteful pitch. With Mohammad Abbas teasing the ball off the surface and the athletic Mohammad Rizwan snaffling everything up to the stumps, this was a real challenge of mind and technique.

Lawrence will never win awards for aesthetic beauty but he chose the right balls to put away in a 66-ball unbeaten 50 that stretched England’s lead to 357 at 177 for seven in their second innings. Lawrence settled any wobbles about Pakistan pulling off a miracle recovery.

News.title: Springboks level Greatest Rivalry series with blood-and-thunder victory over All Blacks
News.content:
South Africa aim to bounce back from losing the first game of the Greatest Rivalry Tour as they take on New Zealand in game two from Cape Town. The All Blacks claimed an impressive 33-16 win in game on in Johannesburg last weekend, outscoring South Africa five tries to one. That victory takes New Zealand above South Africa in the world rankings into top spot.

The Springboks know that a defeat today will mean they cannot win the series. They have not lost two consecutive Tests since November 2022. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu has been given the nod to start at fly-half but Handre Pollard has pulled out of the matchday squad due to a calf injury.

“There were a handful of positives and negatives last week, but the main thing that let us down was that we created so many chances, but mistakes at crucial times cost us,” South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus said.

“We will put in a lot of work this week to ensure that we are sharp in that regard this weekend because if we had used even some of those chances, the result could have been completely different. That said, we know New Zealand will be charged up after winning last week, and they will want to build on that. But the key for us will be to focus on our game and ensure that we are as effective as possible all around.”

Sports.title: Wrexham rip up former England star Conor Coady’s contract after playing just six games for club
Sports.content:
WREXHAM have parted ways with former England star Conor Coady after just SIX appearances for the club.

The Championship side confirmed the defender has left the Racecourse Ground by mutual consent just over a year after he joined.



Wrexham wrote on X: “We can confirm that Conor Coady has left the Club following the mutual termination of his contract.

“We wish Conor all the best for the future.”



Coady, 33, joined Phil Parkinson’s side from Leicester last August in a deal worth around £2million.

He signed a two-year contract, with Wrexham holding the option of extending it by another 12 months.



But the move did not work out, with Coady making just five Championship appearances and one in the League Cup.

The centre-back started Wrexham’s first five league games last season before dropping out of Parkinson’s side.

His final appearance came in the 2-1 League Cup defeat to Cardiff in October.

Coady was then sent on loan to Charlton in January in search of more game time.

He made 12 Championship appearances for the Addicks and scored once during his spell at The Valley.

But after returning to Wrexham this summer, Coady did not make one matchday squad this season.

The defender, who is now a free agent, won ten England caps and was part of Gareth Southgate’s squads for Euro 2020 and the 2022 World Cup.

Coady is best known for his eight-year spell at Wolves.

At the West Midlands outfit, he made more than 300 appearances and captained them into the Premier League before later playing for Everton and Leicester.

Sports.title: Tottenham working on shock deal for Tosin Adarabioyo in first transfer between Spurs and Chelsea in 17 YEARS
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM are working on a shock late deal for Tosin Adarabioyo from rivals Chelsea – in case wantaway Kevin Danso leaves.

It would be the first transfer directly involving a senior first-team player between the two clubs for 17 years.

Goalkeeper Carlo Cudicini was the last player to move between the London sides, having left Chelsea for Spurs on a free transfer in January 2009.



Striker Jude Soonsup-Bell, now playing in Thailand, also made the same move in 2023 aged 19 but that was from the Blues academy to Spurs’ Under-21 development team.



Tosin, 28, has fallen down the pecking order at Stamford Bridge and is free to leave after being left out of all three of the matchday squads so far this season by boss Xabi Alonso.

Spurs are hunting around late in the window for a new centre-back after Danso asked to leave.

The Austrian international, 27, is worried about game-time having not started any games so far this season and wants to be a regular starter.

Sunderland had a loan bid rejected last week for Danso but are still in talks with Spurs over a possible late deal.

Danso leaving would not only cause boss Roberto De Zerbi a headache because it would leave no obvious back-up on the right-side of defence behind Jan Paul van Hecke.

But Danso is also a Premier League home-grown player, having come through at Reading and MK Dons.

Losing the ex-Southampton loanee would take De Zerbi’s homegrown contingent down to seven players – one below the minimum required.



Should Spurs bring in ex-Manchester City academy player Tosin, though, that number would go back up to eight.

The number would also be boosted if an ambitious deal for Iliman Ndiaye can be completed as he counts as homegrown too.

Sports.title: ‘What’s he doing?’ ask fans after spotting what Man Utd star Youri Tielemans did during Bruno Fernandes penalty routine
Sports.content:
YOURI TIELEMANS left fans baffled when Bruno Fernandes stepped up to take a penalty in Manchester United’s win over Ipswich.

The Red Devils came from behind to notch a 5-2 victory against the newly-promoted Tractor Boys.

And Tielemans, 29, made his home debut after completing a £35million move from Aston Villa during the summer.



But the midfielder stunned supporters as hat-trick hero Fernandes prepared to take a second half spot-kick.



Eagle-eyed fans spotted Tielemans mimicking his team-mate’s penalty routine on the edge of the box.

The Belgian copied Fernandes’ movement towards the ball before celebrating with the United skipper when he found the back of the net.

Confused fans rushed onto social media when they noticed what Tielemans was up to.



One said: “What’s Tielemans doing?”

Another added: “Never seen that before.”

A third puzzled United fan chimed in: “Synchronised penalty taking.”

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

A fourth noted: “Haha fascinating. Almost like a technique to give the keeper double vision. Love it!”



And a fifth claimed: “Learning from the best.”

United legend Gary Neville poked fun at Ipswich goalkeeper Kjell Scherpen after failing to put Fernandes off.

The Dutchman stood to the right-hand side of his goal as the Red Devils favourite started his run-up.

Scherpen then dived to his left, with newly-crowned PFA Player of the Year Fernandes placing his effort exactly where the Ipswich summer signing was initially standing.



Neville, who was on co-commentary duties at Old Trafford, said: “It seems the only person confused by the goalkeeper’s actions is himself.”

Sports.title: EFL forced to move THREE clashes including Liverpool vs Tottenham Carabao Cup fixture as they launch attack on Uefa
Sports.content:
THE EFL have been forced into major changes to THREE blockbuster fixtures after a Champions League scheduling clash caused chaos.

In a statement, chiefs said they had been left with “no choice” but to rearrange the games.



The headache began after UEFA scheduled Liverpool and Everton to play at home on the SAME night.

Everton’s Carabao Cup third-round clash with Wolves had already been pencilled in for September 9 following talks with local stakeholders.



But UEFA then announced Liverpool’s Champions League showdown with Atletico Madrid for the very same evening.

That was despite rules preventing the two Merseyside clubs from hosting matches on the same night.



EFL chiefs held talks with UEFA on Monday in a bid to find a way around the clash.

But they were told Liverpool’s European fixture would NOT be moved.

That has forced the EFL to rip up its original plans and reshuffle other fixtures instead.

Everton will now host Wolves in Round Three of the Carabao Cup on September 16 at 7.45pm.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Tottenham will travel to Liverpool on September 15 for an 8pm kick-off – also in the Carabao Cup.

And Wolves’ Championship fixture against Portsmouth at the Molineux will NOT be on September 16.

They will instead meet on October 20 at 7.45pm.

In a statement released by the EFL, they launched a blistering attack on the overwhelming accommodations forced on them by UEFA.



It read: “Over recent seasons the League has made a number of changes to accommodate the expansion of UEFA Club competitions.

“A decision which was made without adequate consultation with domestic leagues.

“These changes have included splitting Carabao Cup Round Three ties across two weeks, and implementing draw conditions for Round Three which prevent scheduling conflicts for Clubs playing in the UEFA Champions League and UEFA Europa League.

“This makes UEFA’s unwillingness to cooperate all the more frustrating, not least for the supporters of the five Clubs that will now be inconvenienced as a result.”

Meanwhile, Pompey have come out with their own shock statement as they explained “the knock-on effect” after their Molineux trip had been postponed for a second time.



They said: “Due to the extremely late notice of these changes, Wolves are unable to host the game on the original date of September 9.

Sports.title: Manchester United to make Bruno Fernandes best-paid player with new contract
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED are prepared to make Bruno Fernandes their best-paid player.

Fernandes scored a hat-trick in United’s 5-2 humbling of Ipswich Town four days after he received the PFA Player of the Year award.



The 31-year-old’s existing contract expires next year but the club have the option of an additional year.

United are expected to offer Fernandes fresh terms that would put him on a salary of around £350,000 a week, with his contract extended by a year.



When Fernandes inked new terms with United in 2022 and 2024, the expiry date of his contract was only extended by a year on each occasion but he received a significant pay increase.

Fernandes currently earns around £300,000 a week but has a compelling case to be made United’s highest earner.

The Portugal international claimed the Football Writers’ Association Player of the Year accolade and won an unprecedented fifth Sir Matt Busby Player of the Year award in May.

Fernandes also set a new record for assists in a Premier League campaign in 2025-26 as United rose to third and qualified for the Champions League.

The club were prepared to sell Fernandes to Saudi Pro League side Al Nassr for £80million last year but Ruben Amorim blocked a possible departure.

United took measures earlier this year to prevent any attempts to prise Fernandes from the club and his future has been moot for the best part of a year.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Fernandes indicated that he was open to a return to Portugal or Italy in the latter years of his career in an interview last November, which was considered to be an opening salvo ahead of contract talks.

Although the United have introduced a more disciplined salary structure, there is an acknowledgement that Fernandes should be fairly remunerated.

Marcus Rashford is United’s highest earner on a weekly wage of £325,000 but spent 18 months out on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona.

Fernandes has scored 110 goals in 329 appearances for United since he signed from Sporting Lisbon in January 2020.

Sports.title: Chelsea scrambling to sort out futures of ELEVEN players including Enzo Fernandez before transfer window shuts
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are scrambling to sort out the future of Enzo Fernandez and TEN more players before the transfer window closes.

The Blues are reported to be in talks with representatives of Roma midfielder Manu Kone about a move to Stamford Bridge if Fernandez leaves.



A Kone deal is now thought to be more likely than signing Lamine Camara from Monaco, with Bournemouth’s Adam Scott also on Chelsea’s radar.

But Fernandez is far from the only Blues star in limbo ahead of Tuesday night’s 11pm deadline.



The Chelsea recruitment team are set to be the busiest in the Premier League over the next day and a half, with the focus on trimming Xabi Alonso’s massive squad to a manageable number.

Goalkeeper Robert Sanchez needs to leave after being dropped from the team and replaced by new signing Emi Martinez.

But reports of Spurs being interested in Sanchez feel far-fetched and Tottenham will be more concerned with preventing the Blues hijacking their £60m deal for Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye.

Alonso refused to guarantee Pedro Neto would be staying at the club despite his impressive adaptation to a wing-back role.

Liverpool, who are desperate for a right winger, are being linked with Neto, who has already attracted attention from Saudi Arabia.

Mykhailo Mudryk will almost certainly leave Stamford Bridge on loan.

Sports.title: Liverpool ANNOUNCE Bradley Barcola transfer as he becomes second most expensive signing in Premier League history
Sports.content:
LIVERPOOL have announced the bombshell signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain.

The Reds have forked out an initial £106million for the winger, and another £17m could eventually head to Paris in add-ons.



That takes the total outlay to a dizzying £123m – making Barcola the second-most expensive signing in Premier League history, behind his new £125m team-mate Alexander Isak.

Liverpool now have three of the five most expensive arrivals, with Florian Wirtz costing £116m from Bayer Leverkusen last summer.



But they will take some comfort in having knocked a fair chunk off PSG’s initial £145m asking price for Barcola.

The French international is at his best on the left wing and will compete for minutes in a strong Liverpool attack.



The 23-year-old, who has penned a long-term deal and taken the No29 jersey, said: “It’s a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool. I’m very happy.

“It took a long time but I’m really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play.

“I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it’s one of my biggest dreams in my life.

“It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that’s why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“I had the chance to play twice in this stadium and I saw the atmosphere and how the fans were behind the Liverpool players.

“When I knew about Liverpool’s interest in me, I didn’t ask questions and I knew it was a very big club for me.”

Liverpool announced the move via a series of social media posts on Monday afternoon.

First was a shadowy outline of Barcola in the Anfield tunnel, then came a dramatic video montage narrated by the newcomer, in French, in which he called Liverpool his “new home”.



New Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola has used a combination of Cody Gakpo, Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha on the flanks in his first two Premier League games.

Barcola’s arrival could unlock Gakpo’s move to Manchester City for around £85m.

But there are also suggestions the Anfield hierarchy want another winger – most-likely Ismaila Sarr from Crystal Palace – before letting Gakpo go.

The Reds had been tailing Barcola since the start of the summer but explored other targets before returning to PSG with a concrete offer.

Anfield chiefs saw bids knocked back for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh and Eagles ace Sarr as they scoured the market for reinforcements out wide.

Sports.title: Glimpse into England's future as Ireland ODIs end international summer
Sports.content:
England Women's ODI side will have a different look to it against Ireland, with senior figures rested and new or fringe players handed opportunities.

Captain Nat Sciver-Brunt and batter Danni Wyatt-Hodge are absent as they focus on fitness and injury recovery, while spinner Sophie Ecclestone, seamer Lauren Bell and wicketkeeper Amy Jones are also missing for the three-game series, live on Sky Sports.

When the squad was announced earlier this month, the England press release stated the breather given to senior players was also aimed at "widening and deepening the talent pool" and so some newbies and returnees now have a chance to impress.

England squad for Ireland ODIs Charlie Dean (captain), Maia Bouchier, Alice Capsey, ⁠⁠Kira Chathli, Tilly Corteen-Coleman, Sophia Dunkley, Lauren Filer, Dani Gibson, Jodi Grewcock, Freya Kemp, Ryana MacDonald-Gay, Charis Pavely, Grace Potts, Mady Villiers, Issy Wong

The series starts in Leicester on Tuesday (1pm) before the Midlands roadshow continues in Derby on Thursday (1pm) and then concludes in Worcester on Sunday (10.30am).

One intriguing element will be seeing how Alice Capsey does as wicketkeeper, with the 22-year-old poised to take the gloves despite the presence of uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kira Chathli in the 15-player party.

Image: Jones had a poor T20 World Cup but then scored two Test fifties against India

Capsey was the designated back-up wicketkeeper to Jones at the T20 World Cup squad this summer but now gets a gig as senior glovewoman, one that could potentially turn into a long-term role, particularly with Jones now 33 years of age.

Jones notched twin fifties in England's Test defeat to India at Lord's in July, yet toiled in the T20 World Cup before that, making double figures only once in her last six knocks after starting the competition with a half-century against Sri Lanka.

If Capsey can impress with the gloves - a facet Jones still excels in - and keep scoring runs, too, then Jones' rest could perhaps turn into a more permanent absence.

Dean excited to see Capsey keep wicket England stand-in captain Charlie Dean on Alice Capsey: "She is a bit of a jack-of-all-trades really, "She kept really well in one of the warm-up games before the World Cup and I think that sparked a bit more trust in her ability. That's really exciting. "She works really hard off the pitch, I feel like she's growing in confidence and I'm excited to see how it goes."

Should Dean be permanent England captain?

Another look into the future comes as Charlie Dean captains once again, having done that job admirably during Sciver-Brunt's injury issues this summer, steering the side to T20I series wins over New Zealand and India.

The all-rounder has impressed Sky Sports pundit Simon Doull with her "cricket nous" and leadership ability - Doull even suggested she should become permanent skipper now so Sciver-Brunt can focus on her batting.

Dean will be without some key weapons against Ireland - Bell and Ecclestone leave big voids in the bowling attack - but there are some exciting players to keep an eye on.

Image: Charlie Dean captains England in the absence of Nat Sciver-Brunt

Ecclestone's fellow left-arm spinner, 19-year-old Tilly Corteen-Coleman, should add to her two ODIs and one T20I so far. She was the joint-leading wicket-taker in the recent Hundred competition, with 13.

Off-spinner Mady Villiers is rewarded for her punchy outing in the Test versus India by earning a white-ball recall - she brings spark with bat, ball and in the field.

Accurate seamer Ryana MacDonald-Gay and spin-bowling all-rounder Charis Pavely also return having played a limited amount of international cricket before, including against Ireland in 2024, while left-handed batter Jodi Grewcock is selected again.

Grewcock made scores of three and 10 against New Zealand in June but is a real talent and, as a southpaw, will offer a point of difference if named in the XI.

Image: Jodi Grewcock made her England debut against New Zealand earlier this summer

Uncapped seamer Grace Potts will also hope to star, off the back of an 11-wicket Hundred for Welsh Fire, 12 strikes in the One Day Cup for Lancashire so far this season and a further 11 in just six games for her county in the Vitality Blast.

Dean keen for new-look England to grasp their opportunity

Dean said in her press conference on Monday: "It is a very important series for us. We're facing a really strong Ireland side, they had really good form in the World Cup and they come with a lot of skills.

"We'll be going in with a slightly different bowling attack and it does free up girls to bowl in positions they haven't bowled previously.

Image: Left-arm spinner Tilly Corteen-Coleman (right) is an exciting prospect

"I'm really excited about the squad we have. There are a few girls who will really want to stamp their mark on international cricket and I'm excited to see how we go."

As for captaining the side again, Dean added: "I've had a bit more time to prep and think about it as opposed to it being a bit more of a shock that first time around [against New Zealand].

"Nat is still a huge loss and very much our captain. Hoping I can step in, fill her very big shoes and do a good job for the team.

"Trying to win games of cricket for England and having a bit more influence on that brings a bit more pressure.

"But it's an exciting challenge, with a bit of a different dynamic, and I'll be encouraging the girls to take the opportunity if given to them."

Image: England will be without the rested Nat Sciver-Brunt for the series against Ireland

Sports.title: Munoz reunites with Glasner at Forest after Palace move
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have completed the signing of Daniel Munoz from Crystal Palace.

The deal for the right wing-back is understood to be worth up to £22m.

Munoz, who is reunited with former Palace boss Oliver Glasner at the City Ground, has joined on a three-year deal with the option for a fourth.

Palace opened the door for the 30-year-old's exit by signing Anan Khalaili from Union Saint-Gilloise. They secure a profit on a player they signed from Genk for £8.5m in January 2024.

Colombia international Munoz was a crucial player in Palace's Conference League and FA Cup triumphs.

Image: Munoz has reunited with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest

Munoz told Forest's official website: "I'm really thankful. First of all, to God, for life, for another great opportunity, and to this management which has faith in my skill and my talent.

"I'm really excited and I can't wait to get out on the pitch so I can help my new teammates achieve all the objectives for this season.

"This is a winning club. I think that when this is the expectation, the mentality, both for the management and the technical team, and for the players, this makes it special.

"I think that Oliver Glasner is special, I have a very good relationship with him and we did big things together, it was an incredibly special period. What he did with our previous club, I have a lot of respect and a lot of admiration for him."

Could Henderson join Munoz at Nottingham Forest?

Crystal Palace have no plans to sell any more of their players to Nottingham Forest in the final days of the transfer window.

Last week, a report has emerged of a bid from Forest to sign Palace's goalkeeper and captain Dean Henderson.

But Sky Sports News has been told categorically that Henderson will not be allowed to depart before the deadline.

Palace plan to support new head coach Pierre Sage in the final days of the transfer window.

Are Forest planning anything else before the transfer deadline?

Nottingham Forest could make a late move for Newcastle forward Jacob Murphy.

Image: Newcastle United's Jacob Murphy is a target for Nottingham Forest

Forest are keen on Murphy and are in the market for forwards amid the departure of Omari Hutchinson to AC Milan.

Newcastle have not formally been made aware yet but there is believed to have been interest from Forest earlier in the window, as well as Everton.

Newcastle are looking to add new forward options themselves with interest in Lille's Matias Fernandes Pardo and Stuttgart's Bilal El Khannouss.

Meanwhile, Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Forest to re-sign Arnaud Kalimuendo on loan.

The striker was on loan at the German club for the second half of last season and they now want to do another loan potentially with an option to buy Kalimuendo permanently. He was left out of the matchday 18 on Saturday as Forest drew 2-2 at Liverpool.

Sky Sports News has already reported that Forest's proposed move for Harrison Armstrong from Everton has broken down.

After receiving an approach from Forest, Sky Sports News understands the board is unanimous in its decision to not sell the player.

What else are Palace working on before Deadline Day?

Crystal Palace are now close to an agreement with Atalanta to sign Honest Ahanor on loan.

Sky Sports News understands that the proposal is for Ahanor to join the Eagles on a season-long loan from Atalanta and then join Chelsea permanently next summer.

Chelsea have been in talks to sign him permanently from Atalanta for around £40m. He cannot be loaned from Chelsea to Palace because Axel Disasi is already on loan at Selhurst Park.

In terms of outgoings, Ismaila Sarr wants to leave Palace before the deadline. However, Palace insist the player is still not for sale and he still has a contract until 2029.

Liverpool made an approach for the Senegal international in the past week. He is one of a number of options under consideration at Liverpool, including Yankuba Minteh at Brighton.

Sarr has missed Palace's first two games of the season through injury. The window closes on Tuesday at 11pm.

Sports.title: How Scheffler broke another Tiger record to cap off dominant FedExCup season
Sports.content:
It has taken less than five seasons for Scottie Scheffler to go from being winless on the PGA Tour to breaking Tiger Woods' 26-year-old career money record.

While financial earnings between the two are difficult to compare, given the enormous spikes in prize money since Woods' prime era, it highlights just how dominant Scheffler has been on the PGA Tour to overtake the record so quickly.

Woods' total on the official PGA Tour career money list remains at $120,999,166, having last featured competitively in 2024, while Scheffler broke through the $130m barrier with his impressive Tour Championship victory at East Lake.

A three-shot win over Viktor Hovland saw Scheffler join Woods and Rory McIlroy as the only players with multiple FedExCup titles, with his latest success a third PGA Tour victory of another impressive campaign.

"To come from behind and be able to win the tournament is a really cool feeling," Scheffler said. "There was a lot of talented guys in front of me on the leaderboard. I was fortunate to get off to a good start and put myself in the mix."

Scheffler's Tour Championship triumph means he bookends his season with victories, having started his campaign by claiming The American Express before having a seven-month wait to next find the winner's circle.

Image: Scheffler's season in numbers, where he posted 13 top-four finishes in 20 starts

He ended inside the top four 10 times during that frustrating winless period, with a runner-up finish to Rory McIlroy at The Masters among five seconds, although still entered the FedExCup Playoffs as No 1 for a fifth consecutive season.

Scheffler responded with a dominant eight-shot win at the FedEx St. Jude Championship, the opening FedExCup Playoff event, while his victory at East Lake sees him become just the 31st player to reach 22 career wins on the PGA Tour.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the fourth round of the FedEx St. Jude Championship, where Scheffler dominated

"I felt like my thought process going into (the FedExCup Playoffs) was that maybe I've underperformed in some of the post-seasons in the past," Scheffler said. "I think of 2022 and 2023, where I had a lead at this tournament and wasn't able to win the FedExCup or a Playoff event.

"I came in this year maybe not winning the tournaments that I could have won throughout the regular season, so to come in and win two out of three Playoff events is definitely a nice way to finish off the season."

Image: Scheffler's 22 PGA Tour titles are twice any other player has managed since the start of 2022

It marks the fifth year in a row that Scheffler has won multiple PGA Tour titles, equalling Woods' career-best streak, while he becomes the first player since Dustin Johnson from 2016-18 to claim three or more victories in three consecutive seasons.

"Three wins, five runner-ups and finishing the season No 1 - those are some numbers to be proud of," Woods posted on X. "Incredible consistency all season long. Congrats on a historic season, Scottie."

How Scheffler's 'got an edge' over PGA Tour rivals

Scheffler's strokes-gained stats were nearly a shot a round better than his closest challenger over the PGA Tour season, plus he topped tee-to-green, greens in regulation and scoring average metrics during another super year.

"I think he [Scheffler] knows that he's got an edge on most guys out here." Hovland said. "He doesn't have to do anything crazy. He can play smart and just pick his spots, stay in it constantly.

"Today [Tour Championship], it wasn't like anybody else really played all that great in contention - a lot of guys were just gagging and throwing up. That's where he stays in it and shoots a nice score and that gets the job done."

Only Greg Norman and Woods have had more time as the world No 1 than Scheffler, who holds such a commanding lead over McIlroy and the chasing pack that - regardless of results over the rest of the year - he will start 2027 still in top spot.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the most memorable moments from every PGA Tour winner in 2026, including three victories for Scheffler

Scheffler has been world No 1 since May 2023 but would need to stay there until October 2028 to break Woods' record consecutive stint of 281 weeks at the top, with the four-time major champion keen to keep building on his success.

"I feel like I hold myself to a high standard, which I think sometimes can be good and bad," Scheffler admitted. "I feel like at times I probably could be a bit of a pain to be around when things aren't going the way they should.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Scheffler almost made a hole-in-one on the second hole of his final round at the Tour Championship

"I don't feel like I take days off. I'm highly competitive and I'm very proud of being able to have the consistent results I've had over the years. I feel like it's something that's very difficult to do.

"I don't take days off during tournaments. I try to give it my all each and every day. I feel like it's a gift to play out here on the PGA Tour and don't want to take it for granted.

"I don't want to look back at the end of my career and feel like I could have done more in order to play well. I want to be able to tell myself when I hang it up that I did everything I could. I feel like years like this show to myself how important that is."

Image: Scheffler will have another opportunity to complete the career Grand Slam next summer at the US Open

When a 15-time major champion is using adjectives like 'incredible' and 'historic' to describe your season, you know you are doing something right. With every passing year, Scheffler keeps hitting generational standards not seen since Woods at his best.

What's next?

The PGA Tour takes two weeks off before starting its FedExCup Fall schedule with the inaugural Biltmore Championship from September 17-20, held in Asheville, North Carolina.

Scheffler will feature for Team USA in the Presidents Cup a week later, when they host the International Team at Medinah and chase an 11th consecutive victory in the biennial contest. Get latest Sky Sports deals or stream with no contract on NOW.

Sports.title: 'It's like the first day of school' - Earps on being part of LCL's new superstar squad
Sports.content:
Mary Earps is used to leading from the front, whether as an England goalkeeper or highlighting issues in the women's game. This summer, she was the first one through the door as London City Lionesses collated a star-strewn squad.

The goalkeeper returns to the WSL after a two-year spell in France with PSG, something she describes as 'a very different environment'.

Speaking exclusively to Sky Sports ahead of the WSL's return on September 4, when London City face her former side, Manchester United, Earps said: "I really feel like I was able to go away and work on myself for a couple of years. There were things in my game that I've been able to kind work on as well.

"As a person, living away from home, immersing yourself in a new language, in a new culture, a new city, a new country, it teaches you a lot of things about yourself. It gives you space to reflect and figure out more about who you are and who you want to be as a person."

There's so many things you miss about home. You miss your family and friends. I missed the English mentality and football culture. I don't think there's anything like playing football in England. It's a very special atmosphere with the history of the game, the iconic stadiums and the electricity you feel when you step on the pitch.

Earps has never been afraid of the big move. She also played for German giants Wolfsburg for a year before joining Man Utd and it's that experience that gives her empathy for the players coming to England.

"There's people who are maybe moving clubs for the first time," she said. "There's people moving countries, speaking different languages. I know how hard that is, but even moving back to England and speaking English, it's still a transition."

And the list of players now at London City is eye-watering. The biggest is Alexia Putellas - the Ballon d'Or winner who left her childhood club Barcelona for Bromley. Her team-mate Mapi Leon followed, as has Kadidiatou Diani. That's before we even talk about the players already there, like Kosovare Asllani, Delphine Cascarino and Grace Geyoro.

While these players, Earps included, are used to superstardom, they are still the newbies - dauting for anyone - but such an experience fosters a comradery vital for a successful team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Mary Earps shares why she has decided to join London City Lionesses and lifts the lid on her conversation with majority owner Michele Kang.

The goalkeeper explained: "I feel very much part of the newness of it all, and it's nice when other people are experiencing that for the first time as well, but even the players that have been here before, they've maybe only been here a year or so.

"But that's what happens when you're a brand new entity and it's exciting because you get to be a part of that history, and I do believe that London City will go on to do incredible things for a long time. That's a massive reason why I came here.

"It's great in a way because it's like everyone's first day at school. You say 'oh, I'm so nervous', but everyone is nervous because everyone's doing the same thing.

"But there's a lot of experience in the room as well. A lot of the players have won trophies, have incredible pedigree, so we're all bonded by that experience and maybe bumping into each other or playing against each other in some way.

"I honestly can't speak highly enough of the group that I've experienced so far and they've been brilliant at welcoming me."

It's not yet clear if Earps will be the London City No1. She will likely fight for the shirt alongside last season's first choice, Elene Lete - who signed a new deal this summer - with Sophia Poor and Sophie Hillyerd also among the goalkeeping group.

The goalkeepers have been brilliant with me. We've had a really good working relationship on the pitch. We work hard, we push each other because we all want to play, but we have a laugh in between sets and help each other out as well.

London City will want to tighten up at the back too, conceding 35 WSL goals last season. Not the worst, but for context, the top two - Manchester City and Arsenal - conceded 33 between them. Chelsea only let in 20, and if the club has any ambitions of unseating the Big Three, their number needs to dramatically reduce.

So how does the former WSL Golden Glove winner go about building that solidity with her new defenders?

"It's getting to know them because every individual is so different," Earps explained. "It's a lot of small details which make a big difference.

"Full-back and centre-back are two very different positions. Then you've got everyone's individual qualities and that is probably the hardest part - getting to know things like their starting positions, how they want to do the recovery runs, what position they going to take up in the box or how they like to receive the ball - do they like it in front of them, at them? Are they going to take two steps forward?

Image: Mary Earps was part of the England squad that won Euro 2022 and reach the World Cup final in 2023

"And equally, they've got to get to know me, understand my position and where I like to be, what type of goalkeeper I am, so it's a lot of working it out on the pitch.

"I sometimes grab a conversation over lunch or in between reps and we're bouncing ideas off each other all the time."

London City's first test will come on September 4 as they open the WSL season against Man Utd at Hayes Lane, live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player London City Lionesses' Freya Godfrey speaks about playing alongside Alexia Putellas and Mary Earps, revealing what she has learned from the experienced duo and the lessons she is hoping to take into her own game

Earps' former side have had a turbulent summer, losing key players as well as changing head coach. Former Hearts boss Eva Olid replaced Marc Skinner, who left by mutual consent after five years.

"I was at Man Utd for five years. I have incredible memories there and met some incredible people," Earps said. "I know the club has changed a lot. There's not so many of the faces there that I know, but equally, they still have incredible players.

"It will be a really tough game, but I'm looking forward to it and I love a challenge. The support of Man Utd is always fantastic, home and away, so I know they'll come to Bromley and try and make it a difficult atmosphere for us.

Image: Mary Earps won the FA Cup with Man Utd in 2023

"I don't know the ins and outs of everything, but I won an FA Cup with Marc and I will always really cherish that memory. It gives me goosebumps just thinking about it, to be honest.

"He also helped the club get to three other finals, so I think that speaks for itself and I wish him all the best in his next chapter."

Now though, Earps focus is on her own new chapter and another landmark chapter for London City. It remains to be seen how this headline-grabbing summer will translate onto the pitch - but it's one neither fans, nor the players, will forget in a hurry.

Sports.title: 'He belongs at the top of the game' - Fery faces world No 14 Musetti at US Open
Sports.content:
British star Arthur Fery faces a tough task when he goes up against 13th seed Lorenzo Musetti on Tuesday at the US Open

Fery returned to British No 1 and set a new career high at No 33 following his run to the Winston-Salem Open final this week. His hopes of landing his maiden ATP Tour title were ended in emphatic fashion by Ignacio Buse on Saturday.

The 24-year-old was aiming to add to his already memorable season having reached the semi-finals at Wimbledon but he was denied by the Peruvian.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Winston-Salem Open final between Arthur Fery and Ignacio Buse

Eight weeks ago, Fery was outside the top 100.

Despite missing out on the title, Fery will take plenty of confidence from a week that yielded five consecutive straight-set victories and further underlined his potential on the ATP Tour.

The Brit will now switch his attention to the US Open, where he is set to make his main draw debut in New York.

He faces a tough first-round clash against Musetti, but his recent form suggests he will arrive in Flushing Meadows full of belief and confidence.

Sports.title: Football transfer deadline day looms: Liverpool sign Barcola, Chelsea target Koné, and more – live
Sports.content:
2m ago 11.04 EDT Jacob Steinberg Brighton are pushing to complete a deal for Millwall’s Femi Azeez. Millwall want £15m for the forward, who was in the Championship team of the season last year. Brighton are yet to meet the 25-year-old’s valuation but there is an expectation the deal will go through. Share

17m ago 10.48 EDT Jamie Jackson Manchester United are open to loans for the Harry Amass, their 19-year-old left-back, who joined from Watford in 2023, and Chido Obi, the 18-year-old striker, who signed two years ago from Arsenal. The pair are on the periphery at Old Trafford right now. Share

25m ago 10.41 EDT This is a bit of a shock. Karim Benzema and his club Al-Hilal have mutually agreed to terminate his contract. Benzema, now 38, joined the Saudi Pro League club in February this year after spending three years with Al-Ittihad. It has been reported that the Frenchman will announce his decision on his future soon, although a return to a European club is believed to be unlikely; Benzema could retire altogether. Share

35m ago 10.30 EDT Manchester City’s new signing Allan Elias has revealed he chatted to his former Palmeiras teammate Vitor Reis about signing for the club. Reis moved from the Brazilian club to City in January 2025 before heading out on loan to Girona last season and is now embedded within Enzo Maresca’s squad. Allan has now joined him in swapping São Paulo for Manchester. “He [Reis] sent me a message, when there were still some rumours going on,” Allan told the City club website. “We still haven’t talked about what it’s like here, but he said that when I arrived he would give me attention and talk to me and explain to me how it works.” Share

1h ago 10.09 EDT Do Manchester United actually need a left-back? Kevin Wilson is not so sure. double quotation mark Man Utd might be over-egging the LB issue. Clearly Lewis Hall is the preference and he isn’t available but Shaw is going to play most games and Dorgu, Harry Amass and Diego Leon can all cover, let alone Dalot or Mazrouai. Unless someone who can replace Shaw now is available, then save the money. Earlier this month, I wrote about the left-back situation here: Frugal or foolish? Manchester United may regret not backing Carrick Read more Share

1h ago 09.57 EDT I may as well name all those £100m signings now: Alexander Isak – Newcastle to Liverpool, £125m

Morgan Rogers – Aston Villa to Chelsea, £117m

Elliot Anderson – Nott’m Forest to Man City, £116m

Enzo Fernández – Benfica to Chelsea, £106.8m

Bradley Barcola – PSG to Liverpool, £106m (plus £17m add-ons)

Declan Rice – West Ham to Arsenal, £100m (plus £5m add-ons)

Jack Grealish – Aston Villa to Man City, £100m

Florian Wirtz – Leverkusen to Liverpool, £100m (plus £16m add-ons)

Moises Caicedo – Brighton to Chelsea, £100m (plus £15m add-ons) Share Updated at 10.01 EDT

Tosin looks to be well down the pecking order at Chelsea, if not a confirmed ‘bomb squad’ member this summer. Also, the BBC have gazumped my £100m player quiz by naming them all in their live blog – don’t look now! Share

1h ago 09.41 EDT A slight correction from earlier: the Barcola deal will not quite be a British transfer record even if the add-ons are achieved to take it from £106m to £123m. That honour still belongs to the Alexander Isak to Liverpool deal, which was worth £125m. There have now been nine signings by Premier League clubs that have surpassed the £100m mark. Fernandes will be 32 on 8 September. View image in fullscreen Bruno Fernandes celebrates one of his three goals for Manchester United versus Ipswich. 2h ago 09.24 EDT Some Barcola reaction for you, including a pronunciation guide for Manchester City fans: Kev McCready says: “As an LFC fan, Barcola will improve us tremendously. I’ll miss Gakpo, having only just learned how to pronounce his name correctly. It’s been a strange window, with some gaps still remaining and possibly two young players coming in next year (Bruggmans, N’Guessan). It’s HACK-po by the way, City fans.” Krishna: “Regarding Barcola, we once signed one Fernando Torres for a then record transfer fee of £50m and Barry Glendenning later called him a fish for his aversion to find the net.” Share

They also like Monaco’s Lamine Camara and their interest in Bournemouth’s Alex Scott and Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton is no secret. 2h ago 09.07 EDT Thanks Gregg. Doesn’t it feel strange that a Premier League club can pay £123m for a player – a British transfer record – and we can all just collectively shrug? Make no mistake, Barcola is a fine footballer though, it will be fascinating to see how he fares at Anfield. Share

2h ago 09.00 EDT Liverpool sign Barcola from PSG in potential £123m deal Liverpool have completed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain for an initial £106m fee, which could rise to £123m. The France international has signed a five-year deal at Anfield. Andoni Iraola has prioritised signing wingers this summer after replacing Arne Slot. Barcola follows the arrival of Victor Muñoz as the former Bournemouth head coach aims to rebuild the frontline. The 23-year-old was a long-term target for Liverpool who have tracked his progress over a number of seasons. Completing the transfer has been delayed while PSG awaited making their own signings to compensate for Barcola’s exit. The winger attracted interested from other clubs but as adamant that he was only willing to join Liverpool and has ignored other offers. Liverpool have targeted younger players in this window, evidenced by the signings of 21-year-old Jérémy Jacquet and 23-year-old Muñoz in the hope of building a squad for the long-term. Liverpool confirm Bradley Barcola signing from PSG in £123m deal Read more View image in fullscreen Bradley Barcola is unveiled on Merseyside. Photograph: Liverpool FC/Getty Images Share Updated at 09.08 EDT

2h ago 08.51 EDT We have an email from someone who has watched Jamie Jaleel Jeremy Leweling (yep, that’s a great name) far more than I have. “I’ve been a fan of Jamie Leweling since he signed for Stuttgart, so I’m thrilled at the idea of him joining Liverpool,” writes Morgan Blake. “If it had been up to me, Liverpool would have gone in for him last summer. Terrific player.” Bild are now reporting that Roma have now submitted second bid of €35m for the winger, however. Share

2h ago 08.45 EDT Allan has been talking on the Manchester City website about how proud he is to be joining the 10-times champions. double quotation mark This is a surreal moment for me. Manchester City, with everything they have won over the past 15 years, are one of the most attractive clubs in the world for players. To be able to sit here today and say I have joined them is the proudest moment of my life. I love Palmeiras and always will – but the decision to come to City was an easy one. I want to be the best footballer I can be and the conversations I’ve had with the people at City so far has convinced me there isn’t a better place for me to fulfil my ambitions. I want to promise the Manchester City fans I will give absolutely everything to make the most of this opportunity. Now the hard work begins. I will give 100% in training and make the best case possible to the manager I should be playing. My intention is to help City continue winning trophies. If I can do that, it would be a dream come true. View image in fullscreen Allan with Hugo Viana there. Photograph: Tom Flathers/Manchester City FC Doku, Semenyo, Monga, Cherki, Foden and possibly Gakpo. He’ll have a fair bit of competition from forwards/wingers at the Etihad. He is versatile, though. Good luck to the lad. Share Updated at 08.47 EDT

3h ago 08.33 EDT Wingers are so “in” right now and Sky Sport Germany are reporting that Liverpool and Everton are going to battle it out for Stuttgart wide man Jamie Leweling. The 25-year-old Germany international is reportedly also of interest to Roma. Everton have their hands full sorting ins and outs over the next 24 hours, with the Toffees looking to offload Beto and potentially bring back Jack Grealish and Richarlison to the club, as well as finalising a deal for Folarin Balogun. That would be good news for Everton-supporting Andy Burnham – the UK prime minister would then have an easy ice-breaker if he stumbles into Donald Trump at the UN general assembly. Share Updated at 08.36 EDT

3h ago 08.22 EDT Jamie Jackson Claudio Echeverri is expected to be loaned to Benfica by Manchester City for the season. The 20-year-old forward joined in January 2024 from River Plate. The Argentinian has made three City appearances and previously had temporary spells at Bayer Leverkusen and Girona, one of City’s sister clubs. Share Updated at 08.23 EDT

3h ago 08.21 EDT This has been an odd transfer window hasn’t it? Key players going for modest sums. Those who are peripheral or surplus-to-requirements heading out for big money. It’s made the length of contracts seem more important than ever. It’s little wonder some players are forever scrawling their signatures on longer deals. Share

3h ago 08.16 EDT Jacob Steinberg Sunderland are interested in a deal for the Lyon winger Malick Fofana. The 21-year-old Belgian has two goals in six games this season. Share

3h ago 08.12 EDT Thanks Dom. Hello folks. Let’s get this lunchtime stint started then, eh? And what better way than to focus on a club that has seemingly taken up most of the transfer window’s bandwidth this summer, Tottenham Hotspur! It’s not a big slice of news, to be honest, with talented teenage forward Mikey Moore heading to Köln on loan. There’s no deal in place for a potential sale, which shows that Spurs still value the player and expect him back, perhaps with a little more polish, next summer. And while we’re on the subject of the Bundesliga, read all about Elversberg’s big win at the weekend. They’re the German top flight’s village people, in case you were wondering. Elversberg and ‘miracle village’ prove that Bundesliga fairytales still exist | Andy Brassell Read more Share

3h ago 08.06 EDT Manchester City sign Allan in £34m deal Jamie Jackson Manchester City have confirmed the signing of Allan Elias from Palmeiras in a €37.5m plus €2.5m (£34m) deal. The 22-year-old wide forward made his senior debut for Palmeiras last year and has made 96 appearances for the club, scoring nine goals and making 12 assists. Allan is City’s third major acquisition of the window following Elliot Anderson, for £116m, and Ayyoub Bouaddi, for £85m. City are open to a loan for Jack Grealish, with Everton hopeful of taking the 30-year-old. View image in fullscreen Allan signs for Manchester City. Photograph: Tom Flathers/Manchester City FC Share Updated at 08.39 EDT

3h ago 08.02 EDT And on that bombshell, I shall hand over to Gregg Bakowski for the next hour. Plenty more transfer news to come! Share

3h ago 08.01 EDT Muñoz signs for Forest in £22m transfer from Palace Ben Fisher Nottingham Forest have added a key component: Daniel Muñoz has reunited with Oliver Glasner after signing in a £22m deal from Crystal Palace. One of Glasner’s priorities this window was a right-wing back. The 30-year-old Colombia international, part of Palace’s Conference League and FA Cup triumphs under Glasner, has signed a three-year contract, with the option of a further 12 months. Muñoz could make his Forest debut at home to Tottenham on Saturday. View image in fullscreen Daniel Muñoz has reunited with Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest. Photograph: Silvina Brodersohn/CameraSport/Getty Images Share

3h ago 07.52 EDT Will Unwin Burnley defender Joe Worrall is closing in on a move to Championship rivals Wrexham after the clubs agreed a fee in the region for £2m. The centre-back has never become a regular at Turf Moor and is expected to sign a three-year deal with at the Racecourse Ground. Burnley could move for a centre-back to replace him, and have previously been interested in Galatasaray’s Victor Nelsson, who is available for free. Share

3h ago 07.46 EDT Hull and Ipswich may already have Premier League wins under their belts, but the two promoted teams are not done when it comes to incoming transfers. And it seems they are targeting the best Championship talent, a pretty standard move for newly-promoted sides. Sky are reporting that Hull have agreed a deal to sign Sorba Thomas from Stoke – but that the Potters want to find a replacement before sanctioning the winger’s exit – while Ipswich, according to TeamTalk, are closing in on Burnley striker Zian Flemming. Share

3h ago 07.37 EDT An email from David Wall on one of Liverpool’s many current issues: double quotation mark Is one of Liverpool’s main problems that they’ve been thinking for so long about finding a partner for Van Dijk that they didn’t really think about finding a replacement for him? If it wasn’t already clear at times last season, it should be from the start of this. He’s far from the player he was even in Liverpool’s recent title-winning year and is often the source of their defensive problems now (with lack of pace and subsequent poor positioning) rather than the solution to them. I think that’s a very smart observation, David. But a centre-back doesn’t appear to be on Liverpool’s shortlist for the immediate term. Share

4h ago 07.32 EDT Chelsea: It’s genuinely hard to keep track of Chelsea’s ever-changing squad and it should be of no surprise to anyone that the Blues look likely to conduct more business before tomorrow’s deadline. Xabi Alonso’s side may have to accommodate for the departure of Enzo Fernández, who could join Manchester City, so have Lamine Camara – also linked with Liverpool – and Roma’s French midfielder Manu Koné on their shortlist of replacements. Chelsea have already signed Valentín Barco and Jordan Henderson to boost their midfield numbers this summer, with Moises Caicedo and Roméo Lavia among Alonso’s first choices. It’s another Rubik’s Cube of transfer possibilities Chelsea will have to unscramble in the next day or so. View image in fullscreen It is likely that Enzo Fernández will leave Chelsea. Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty Images Share Updated at 07.46 EDT

4h ago 07.17 EDT Jamie Jackson Manchester United have spent £150m overhauling their midfield this summer, yet their standout midfield player in the 5-2 thumping of Ipswich came free from the pitches of Cheadle, Stockport – academy product Kobbie Mainoo. Harry Maguire waxed lyrical about Mainoo after the 21-year-old all-round stellar midfield display at Old Trafford on Sunday. The defender said: “I thought he was brilliant, Kobbie. To say he hasn’t played for I don’t know how long – not really got many minutes in pre-season and things like that, he was magnificent. He put a great shift in and I think his work without the ball has improved so much since Michael [Carrick, the manager] has been in. “That’s probably credit to Michael and his staff. But I think without the ball now, he’s becoming a real monster in there, and he wins a lot of second balls. He wins a lot of duels. You won’t want to play against him in there and that’s the biggest compliment I can give to him from playing and watching him behind. “He’s so young, if we want him to play for this club for another 10 years, there’s going to be times where he’s going to go through a patch like with Rashy and myself, but that’s part and parcel. I think he’s really level-headed, he’s really composed, he has great belief in his ability and, he’s going to be a magnificent play for this club for many, many years.” Share

4h ago 07.11 EDT Toby Podmore weighs in on email with some ‘amusing transfer banter’ – his words: double quotation mark Concerning your post at 11hr50, what’s the going price for selling Jesus these days? I imagine that inflation has made 30 pieces of silver highly uncompetitive. Share

4h ago 07.06 EDT Manchester City fan Sean Baker responds to the question from Liverpool fan Graeme about the prospect of signing Cody Gakpo: double quotation mark I’m excited by the prospect of Gakpo joining. He’s been very consistent in the Premier League – won the league, has Champions League experience, and has scored goals at the Euros and World Cup. Is he the most exciting winger in the world right now? No, probably not. But I think he offers great versatility, something not all wingers can provide. He primarily plays on the left, but can do a good job as a striker, and seems like he’s not shabby on the right

wing either. This means he can play across the entire front three and will be a great backup to Haaland/Doku/Semenyo. With City in the mix for four different competitions, he’s going to get plenty of minutes, and I’m pretty confident he’ll be able to deliver. Yes, £85m is not cheap, and many will argue it’s way too much for a player that’s not a nailed-on starter – but I think he’d be great and would be keen to see him join. Share

4h ago 07.00 EDT These Unai Emery quotes have sparked a fair bit of debate, as the Spaniard was asked about Aston Villa’s relationship with Chelsea given the players that have moved between the clubs this summer and in recent years. Emi Martinez and Morgan Rogers have joined the Blues from Villa, with Alejandro Garnacho heading the other way. Last year, Villa signed Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea and in 2024 paid £37.5m to sign Ian Maatsen from the west Londoners. Emery said: “Good relations? They want to kill us and we want to kill them!” “We have good players and we can sign one player off them, it’s not a good relationship – it’s a deal for money and a deal for players. I am happy for Emiliano Martinez and Morgan Rogers and I know I am not happy for Chelsea.” View image in fullscreen Tell us what you really think, Unai. Photograph: Leonhard Simon/UEFA/Getty Images Share

4h ago 06.50 EDT Arsenal agree to sell Jesus, Martinelli and Vieira Arsenal are running out of time to persuade Julián Alvarez to join them from Atlético Madrid after agreeing to sell Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Fábio Vieira in deals collectively worth more than £70m. Ed Aarons has the skinny from the Emirates – it seems even the champions could be busy between now and 11pm tomorrow. Arsenal trying to lure Julián Alvarez after agreeing deals to sell Martinelli and Jesus Read more Share Updated at 06.59 EDT
