He can commit any number of fouls and can be reinstated after a phone call from one vain man to another.” I wonder what that’s in reference to … Share

4h ago 06.40 EDT As per our man Jacob Steinberg earlier, West Ham have now announced and confirm the arrival of Edvin Austbø from Viking. The deal is worth about £10m. How much more business will the Hammers do in an effort to supercharge their promotion campaign? Share

5h ago 06.32 EDT Manchester City Women sign Leverkusen's Wamser Tom Garry Manchester City Women have signed the Germany full-back Carlotta Wamser from Bayer Leverkusen on a four-year contract. The 22-year-old is the defending WSL champions’ third signing of the summer so far, after the England internationals Beth Mead and Niamh Charles. Wamser, who has 14 senior caps and was part of Germany’s squad at 2025’s Euros, told Manchester City’s media channels: “The English league is the best league in the world and Manchester City is one of the best clubs in the world. I feel like I need the next step for my career and I feel that I can develop as a player here.” City’s director of football Therese Sjögran said: “We are delighted to welcome Carlotta to the Club. She is a player we’ve admired for some time and know she will bring energy, passion and a willingness to learn to the team. For such a young, exciting talent to trust us with the next step of her career is something we feel conveys a strong message of what we are building here at City.” View image in fullscreen Carlotta Wamser poses with Therese Sjogran after signing for Manchester City. Photograph: Man City Share Updated at 06.59 EDT

5h ago 06.24 EDT Fiorentina have reportedly agreed a deal to sign Willy Gnonto on loan from Leeds, with a medical booked on Tuesday. The Italian winger has had a curious spell at Elland Road. He began like a house on fire, then drifted in and out of the team, finding himself as a substitute more often than not last season. Perhaps a fresh start for the 22-year-old is necessary. Share

5h ago 06.17 EDT Liverpool fans are getting a little angsty ahead of the transfer window’s final days and we’ve had this email from Graeme Neill: double quotation mark I’m not exactly going to be sorry to see the back of Richard Hughes. Our transfer strategy over the last few seasons has been chaotic. Why we sold both Jones and Quansah remains baffling. We overpaid for Isak and, unlike Muñoz, he hasn’t felt like the kind of relatively bargain buy that defined the late 2010s. And the less said about his pre-season last year and corresponding fitness issues, the better. Unless Barcola can be reinvented as Fabinho circa 2019, it’s hard to get too excited about him either. I am genuinely curious how excited City fans are about the prospect of Gakpo though. Manchester City fans, get in touch: would you be excited to see Cody Gakpo as part of your frontline? Share

5h ago 06.10 EDT Some slightly lower-key deals for you: Rotherham United have confirmed the signing of Manchester United youngster Jayce Fitzgerald on loan for the rest of the season.

Barcelona have signed 16-year-old prodigy Mikael Baza from Hamburg – he will join their youth ranks.

Jaden Heskey is to return to Sheffield Wednesday from Manchester City on loan after impressing last season. We’ll keep you updated with more deals like this throughout the day. Share Updated at 06.17 EDT

5h ago 05.52 EDT It’s turning into quite an interesting window for Everton. Balogun should be an upgrade on Beto up front, while David Moyes has sounded quite confident about Thierno Barry’s progress at the start of his second season in English football – always a crucial point in a player’s development. How much game time Barry gets if and when Balogun arrives will be interesting. Losing Ndiaye would be a loss but Richarlison is beloved on the blue side of Merseyside and a fine left-wing replacement if that deal from Spurs happens, while there is still talk of a possible second loan for Jack Grealish. Share

5h ago 05.36 EDT Re: Liverpool’s transfer strategy, here is our correspondent Andy Hunter writing in today’s 10 talking points from week’s Premier League games: double quotation mark It underlines the strangeness of Liverpool’s recent transfer strategy that the understandable excitement generated by Bradley Barcola’s impending £123m arrival from Paris Saint-Germain is offset by concern over the gaps in Iraola’s squad that have not been filled – right-wing, right-back and central midfield being the most obvious ones. The need to improve in all three departments was evident as Liverpool had to fight back to salvage a late 2-2 draw [against Nottingham Forest]. “We don’t know what the squad is going to be on 2 September,” said Iraola, surely holding out hope that wingers are not the only incomings before Tuesday. “I think every analysis I can make is when I know and when everything finishes, when I will know who is going to be here all the season or until January.” View image in fullscreen Will Andoni Iraola get the new signings he needs before the deadline? 6h ago 05.27 EDT Jacob Steinberg West Ham: The Hammers are closing on a deal to sign the Viking winger Edvin Austbø for about £10m. The Championship club have also submitted an offer to sign Ryan Giles on loan with an option to buy, but Hull do not want to lose the left-back. Share

6h ago 05.20 EDT Ollie Watkins has gone from Aston Villa to the Saudi Pro League to join Al-Hilal, and the England striker will be thrown straight into a big game against Al-Ahli and faces the highest of expectations – against fellow Three Lions forward hopeful, Ivan Toney. John Duerden reports on the two English strikers vying for Thomas Tuchel’s attention from the gulf. Watkins faces Toney clash as strikers push for Saudi supremacy and Tuchel’s attention Read more View image in fullscreen Ivan Toney and Ollie Watkins there. Composite: Getty Images Share Updated at 05.36 EDT

6h ago 05.15 EDT Liverpool: Why do the Reds want to sell Cody Gakpo, I hear you ask? It’s a good question as Gakpo, despite some criticism from fans at times, has been pretty consistent during his three-and-a-half years at Anfield, scoring 51 goals in around 180 appearances for Liverpool, playing almost exclusively on the left wing. The departure of Mohamed Salah, plus the signing of Victor Muñoz, the emergence of Rio Ngumoha and the pending arrival of Bradley Barcola have all contributed to a situation where Liverpool believe selling Gakpo and reinvesting the cash would be a wise move. Ngumoha, Muñoz and Barcola are all better on the left flank, where Gakpo likes to play, while Liverpool have right-sided forwards – such as Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh and Ismaïla Sarr of Crystal Palace – on their radar. It seems Liverpool want to address the balance of their attack and Gakpo is the fall guy. Still, selling to Manchester City, as has been suggested, would be surprising. Big clubs don’t like to sell first team players to their rivals. Share Updated at 05.20 EDT

Sports.title: Arsenal trying to lure Julián Álvarez after agreeing deals to sell Martinelli and Jesus
Sports.content:
Arsenal are running out of time to persuade Julián Álvarez to join them from Atlético Madrid after agreeing to sell Gabriel Martinelli, Gabriel Jesus and Fábio Vieira in deals collectively worth more than £70m.

Álvarez has his heart set on Barcelona despite Atlético’s insistence they will not sell to their La Liga rivals and returned to training on Sunday after being left out of their squad for the win over Sevilla. Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta is understood to have spoken to Álvarez last week in an effort to persuade the former Manchester City forward to return to the Premier League and to have been informed the Argentina international wants only Barcelona.

The Spanish champions have since agreed an £8.6m deal to sign Jesus, who has entered the final year of his contract after falling down the pecking order behind Kai Havertz and Viktor Gyökeres. However, Barcelona would like to sign another attacker after selling Ferran Torres to Paris Saint-Germain and are said to have not given up on Álvarez.

Atlético have agreed a deal with Juventus for Jonathan David on an initial loan with an option to make the Canada forward’s move permanent next summer. But they are understood to be determined to keep Álvarez, who joined from City in 2024

Arsenal remain hopeful the 26-year-old could change his mind but are believed to be monitoring several other attacking options. Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye was among the players on their shortlist but Tottenham are in advanced talks over a £60m deal for the Senegal forward. Arsenal missed out on Morgan Rogers to Chelsea and failed in an ambitious attempt to sign Vinícius Júnior, the Brazil forward signing a contract extension at Real Madrid.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Arsenal have signed Christos Tzolis to replace Leandro Trossard on the left but Martinelli’s expected departure to Al-Hilal for a club-record £56m sale would create a space in the squad, although Eberechi Eze is also capable of playing there. Martinelli, who scored six times in the Champions League last season but only once in the Premier League, is due to have his medical on Monday after being left out of Arsenal’s squad against Coventry on the opening weekend. His fee surpasses the £40m Liverpool paid Arsenal for Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain in 2017.

Sports.title: Transfer latest: Juventus in Woltemade loan talks, Everton pushing for Balogun
Sports.content:
Nick Woltemade is close to a loan move from Newcastle to Juventus, a year after arriving at St James’ Park in a club-record £69m deal from Stuttgart.

The gifted Germany forward has struggled to impose himself amid the high-intensity gameplans choreographed first by Eddie Howe and now Matthias Jaissle.

Juventus are one of a handful of clubs – Borussia Dortmund are among the others – to have inquired about Woltemade’s availability and Newcastle are in negotiations with the Turin club regarding a move involving a loan fee of about £5m.

Any switch for the 24-year-old appears contingent on Matias Fernandez-Pardo completing a prospective £51m move from Lille. The 21-year-old Belgium international was top of Jaissle’s shopping list and is due in Newcastle for a medical. He can play across the front line, including as a No 10.

Woltemade is unlikely to be the only player leaving before Tuesday night’s deadline. The winger Jacob Murphy is wanted by Nottingham Forest, Nick Pope – Jaissle’s third-choice goalkeeper – is looking for a new club and Besiktas retain an interest in Joe Willock.

Pope, who started last season as Howe’s first choice and harboured then-realistic ambitions to be part of England’s World Cup squad, wants first-team football after falling behind the new signings Lukas Hornicek and Ewen Jaouen.

Willock has impressed Jaissle and, despite offers from Istanbul, an exit that looked inevitable under Howe may be postponed.

Everton are in talks with Monaco over a deal to sign the striker Folarin Balogun after agreeing to sell Beto to Fiorentina. The United States international has attracted interest all summer after impressing at the World Cup, where he gained notoriety for having his red card punishment suspended after an intervention from Donald Trump.

Although born in New York, Balogun was brought up in London and started his career at Arsenal. He made 10 senior Arsenal appearances, and had loans at Middlesbrough and Reims, before being sold in 2023 to Monaco, where he was the player of the year last season after scoring 13 goals in 30 Ligue 1 appearances.

Balogun is regarded as a replacement for Beto, who is due to undergo a medical with Fiorentina after an offer of about £15m was accepted.

View image in fullscreen Folarin Balogun (right) was in the World Cup spotlight after having his red card punishment suspended. Photograph: Jeff Chiu/AP

Manchester City have confirmed the signing of Allan Elias from Palmeiras in a €37.5m (£32.1m) plus €2.5m deal. The 22-year-old wide forward made his debut for Palmeiras last year and has made 96 appearances for the club, scoring nine goals and making 12 assists.

Allan is City’s third major acquisition of the window after Elliot Anderson, for £116m, and Ayyoub Bouaddi, for £85m. City are open to a loan for Jack Grealish, with Everton hopeful of taking the 30-year-old.

“This is a surreal moment for me,” Allan said. “Manchester City, with everything they have won over the past 15 years, are one of the most attractive clubs in the world for players. To be able to sit here today and say I have joined them is the proudest moment of my life.”

Crystal Palace are poised to sign the Atalanta defender Honest Ahanor on loan. The 18-year-old will join Chelsea on a permanent deal for £40m next summer but is due to gain experience of English football by spending this season at Palace.

Palace have signed Axel Disasi on loan from Chelsea so would not have been able to borrow Ahanor if he had completed his transfer to Stamford Bridge during this window.

Palace have had a disappointing start, losing their first two games under Pierre Sage, and face an uncertain end to the window. Nottingham Forest have completed the £22m signing of the Colombia wing-back Daniel Muñoz from Palace, reuniting him with Oliver Glasner, but have had a bid for Dean Henderson rejected. Liverpool are monitoring the Senegal winger Ismaïla Sarr but Palace are determined not to sell Sarr or the midfielder Adam Wharton, who is of interest to Chelsea.

Hull are interested in taking Dário Essugo on loan from Chelsea. The midfielder joined from Sporting last summer but is not part of Xabi Alonso’s plans.

Sports.title: Fiorentina’s Serie A renaissance feels a way off after chastening centenary | Nicky Bandini
Sports.content:
Fiorentina’s 100th birthday party had been going for four days, starting with a fan procession through the historic centre of Florence on Wednesday night and extending to their home game against Frosinone on Saturday afternoon. The club was founded on 29 August 1926, but a decades-old discrepancy in the reporting of that date has led supporters to celebrate traditionally on the 26th.

This time they started a few hours earlier, gathering in their thousands beneath the marble façade of the Basilica of Santa Maria Novella on the evening of 25 August and building to a firework show beside the river Arno at midnight. The club’s president, Giuseppe Commisso, stopped by to give a speech. At least one former player, Borja Valero, was among the crowd.

In the days that followed, historic monuments across the city were lit up in purple to match Fiorentina’s home strip. They have worn that colour since 1929, having played their first three years in shirts half red and half white. A limited-edition replica of those original tops, priced at €180, sold out in less than two hours.

Fiorentina’s players would wear them against Frosinone. Before kick-off, the club hosted some of their greatest former players and coaches for a lunch at their headquarters in Viola Park. The likes of Gabriel Batistuta, Rui Costa, Adrien Mutu and Cesare Prandelli gathered to eat and then head to the stadium, where they were greeted with a party atmosphere.

Not every preparation had gone to plan. Fiorentina had intended for renovations to their Stadio Artemio Franchi to be completed in time for this occasion, but delays meant the Curva Fiesole – the stand traditionally occupied by ultras – remains closed. Still, those same groups arranged a striking choreography at the opposite end instead, recreating the original club badge against a sea of purple flags.

Spirits were high. Despite an opening 4-0 drubbing by Roma, Fiorentina’s supporters had reasons to believe their team was on a good track. They had spent more than €120m on refreshing their squad with exciting young talent, including the Ivory Coast midfielder Christ Inao Oulaï and highly-rated teenage defender Víctor Valdepeñas from Real Madrid Castilla, as well as Arthur Atta and Mateo Pellegrino, coming off breakout seasons with Udinese and Parma.

View image in fullscreen Choreography by Fiorentina fans before kick-off. Photograph: Andrea Martini/NurPhoto/Shutterstock

And that’s not to mention the players they landed on loan. Real Madrid paid €45m to sign the Argentinian winger Franco Mastantuono from River Plate last August and now the 19-year-old would be lining up in Fiorentina’s attack. Radu Dragusin and Álex Jiménez brought Premier League experience from Tottenham and Bournemouth.

The new manager, Fabio Grosso, would need time to blend this group together. But a home game against newly-promoted Frosinone seemed a perfect opportunity for new faces to establish themselves while marking the club’s centenary in style.

It did not work out that way.

Fiorentina started well enough. After a clumsy first few minutes they began to dictate, Mastantuono on the right taking turns with Albert Gudmundsson on the left at getting behind the defence. Jiménez supported ably with overlapping runs from full-back. It felt like a matter of time before they scored.

But a warning arrived in the 25th minute, when Frosinone launched a counter from a Fiorentina free-kick. They reached the penalty area with a numbers advantage, three on two, but Seydou Fini dallied and got dispossessed as he checked back.

Frosinone’s centre-forward, Antonio Raimondo, roared in frustration. A minute later, he opened the scoring. This time Giorgi Kvernadze drove to the goal-line down the left, barely keeping the ball in, before cutting it back for Raimondo to force home at the near post.

Fiorentina responded well. Atta forced a save from Lorenzo Palmisani, before Mastantuono and Valdepeñas smacked shots against the left post. There were moments of quality. Mastantuono did outrageously well to salvage a ball played behind him, controlling with one heel, then knocking the ball across his defender with the second. The stadium appealed for a penalty as he went to ground under contact from Gabriele Bracaglia, but Mastantuono bounced back to his feet and nutmegged another opponent as he shot against the far upright.

Narrow margins. Instead of pulling level, Fiorentina fell further behind in the 38th minute when Bracaglia headed home from a corner. Now the wind truly came out of their sails. Despite a series of substitutions, Grosso’s team offered no hint of a comeback. Raimondo made it 3-0 to Frosinone in the 68th minute with a glorious chest-down and outside-of-the-boot finish.

View image in fullscreen Mateo Pellegrino holds the ball after a Frosinone goal. Photograph: Claudio Giovannini/EPA

An astonishing scoreline. Frosinone only narrowly avoided relegation to Italy’s third tier in 2025, when they were set to contest a play-out with Salernitana before a points deduction for Brescia bumped them up the Serie B standings. La Gazzetta dello Sport predicted them to struggle again last season, but their manager, Massimiliano Alvini used the pink paper as motivation, showing it off to players at the start of what became an unexpected run to promotion.

There is much more to say about Frosinone, and Alvini, whose only previous experience in Serie A was a winless 18-game stretch with Cremonese four years ago. An unassuming character, who even now maintains an active LinkedIn page but who has earned his place after finding continuous work as a manager – albeit mostly in the lower divisions – for a quarter of a century.

It is hard to move past Fiorentina as the story, however, on the weekend that they marked their centenary by making their worst-ever start to a Serie A season. They have lost their first two games now by a combined seven goals. It is the first time they have begun a top-flight campaign being shut out in back-to-back defeats.

Quick Guide Serie A results Show Milan 2-0 Venezia, Sassuolo 2-1 Torino, Monza 2-3 Udinese, Fiorentina 0-3 Frosinone, Juventus 2-0 Parma, Napoli 1-2 Como, Lazio 1-0 Genoa, Cagliari 0-1 Inter Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Perhaps this will all prove an aberration. We are still a way off yet from the horrors of last season, when Fiorentina took six points from their opening 15 matches, winning none. But this was certainly not the night Giuseppe Commisso wanted. His father, Rocco, had sought to transform Fiorentina after taking the club over in 2019, investing heavily to create what has been billed as Italy’s biggest sports centre at Viola Park, with upgraded training facilities for Fiorentina’s men’s and women’s teams, as well as their academy.

Since Rocco passed away in January, Giuseppe has spoken of wanting to carry forward his father’s legacy. “Our family’s total financial commitment to Fiorentina is €1.1bn,” he said on Saturday. “This summer Fiorentina made the largest single transfer window investment in new players in the history of the club.”

View image in fullscreen The post-game show inside the Stadio Artemio Franchi. Photograph: Image Photo Agency/Getty Images

He was speaking from the pitch, part of a post-game show to mark the centenary. An event that could not escape the shadow of the 90 minutes that preceded it. Many fans did stay to applaud Batistuta, Rui Costa and other club legends who came out for reintroductions and reminiscences. But the current team were drowned in whistles.

“Today, on Fiorentina’s 100th anniversary, I am not declaring that we have arrived, I am declaring that we have begun again,” said Commisso, swapping between English and Italian. “From this fresh start, Fiorentina’s Renaissance will commence.”

All words that fans love to hear. And all a little harder to buy into, in the aftermath of yet another chastening setback.

Sports.title: Elversberg and ‘miracle village’ prove that Bundesliga fairytales still exist | Andy Brassell
Sports.content:
Friday night was no first day fun for VfB Stuttgart as they got first-hand proof of what the rest of the Bundesliga feared: that Bayern Munich are perhaps mightier than ever. The curtain-raiser, though, didn’t actually set the tone for the the weekend. German football has long insisted there is more to their elite league than a title race, and now they have a story that shows the world that surprise and wonder does indeed live here too.

Bayer Leverkusen arrived into their opening fixture of the campaign thinking their season might contain greater certainty than the last one, a more tranquil voyage after being blown off course by almost €300m of player sales and the ill-fated appointment of Erik ten Hag. Enter SV Elversberg, Bundesliga first-timers and representatives of – a “miracle village” as Bild put it – Spiesen-Elversberg, a town with a population of just over 13,000, situated 15km north-east of Saarbrücken, 30 minutes’ drive from the French border.

The miracle got big enough for all to see it on the Bundesliga’s inaugural Saturday afternoon. Seventy minutes into their top-flight debut and the locals gathered in the Ursapharm Arena – currently under a renovation programme to bring it up to a modest 15,000 capacity, with journalists covering the game from a temporary steel gantry on top of scaffolding and accordingly given a safety briefing beforehand – were pinching themselves. Vincent Wagner’s team led 3-0, courtesy of two goals in the space of 60 seconds in the opening 10 minutes, and then a third 25 seconds after half-time.

View image in fullscreen Elversberg players – and mascot – celebrate in front of their home fans after the 3-2 win against Leverkusen. Photograph: Thilo Schmülgen/Reuters

New Leverkusen coach Carles Martínez, who looked increasingly exasperated on the touchline as the game went on, threw a host of forwards on to salvage the game, and Patrick Schick and Christian Kofané both scored to reduce the arrears, but it wasn’t enough. A town with no train station and no town hall was now home to a team not only with a first-day Bundesliga win (and no team from Saarland had won a top-flight game since 1993 when FC Saarbrücken beat – you guessed it – Leverkusen), but a victory over the 2024 champions, no less. Even arriving in the same division was akin to a “moon landing”, Wagner had said before the game, continuing to say staying up would be their “mission to Mars”. August results may be notoriously fickle and this may seem like years ago by November, but the win was no fluke.

And make no mistake, Leverkusen were shook from minute one. Elversberg pressed and rattled them, with the visitors’ new captain Edmund Tapsoba looking more the Bundesliga debutant, prone as Lukas Petkov opened the scoring and then turning over the ball almost from kick-off, as Cole Campbell swept into the area to bludgeon in a quickfire second.

The Bulgarian midfielder Petkov had led from the front in the promotion campaign, scoring 13 and creating another six to pick up the slack after top scorer Younes Ebnoutalib left for Eintracht Frankfurt in the winter break. True to form, Petkov also created David Mokwa’s goal at the start of the second half, which turned out to be the difference with a delicious delivery from the right. Yet Campbell is really indicative of the step up. Bought from Borussia Dortmund for €6m in the summer, the 20-year-old from Houston has been rated for a while without truly making a dent in the top tier, either at BVB or on loan at Hoffenheim. He started here – as much of his team did – like a man on a mission, and having laid out a record fee, Elversberg need this to work too.

View image in fullscreen Elversberg fans celebrate during their team’s opening-day win. Photograph: Christian Kaspar-Bartke/Bundesliga/Getty Images

This spend needs to be put in perspective, of course. When Strasbourg full-back Guéla Doué (elder brother of Desiré) completes his move to the BayArena on Monday, it will be the fourth time this summer that Die Werkself have spent in excess of €20m on a player. Leverkusen, and their coach, had no excuses. After an encouraging pre-season, they were beset by many of the old problems that undercut their Champions League hopes last season. Mark Flekken, their refreshingly blunt goalkeeper, could have been talking in March or May when he told the media: “I can’t even offer an explanation right now.”

On the other side, it was all joy. Flekken’s opposite number Nicolas Kristof, whose brilliant save from Jonas Hofmann in stoppage time shut down Leverkusen’s last hope of taking something from the game, was one of two players in the lineup who has been at the club since they were in the regional fourth tier, winning promotion to the 3.Liga in 2022, at the end of his debut season at the club. It is already a fairytale. If they can build on their start as they build that main stand, it would be a story for the Bundesliga ages.

Quick Guide Bundesliga results Show Bayern Munich 5-1 Stuttgart, Union Berlin 3-3 Eintracht, Leipzig 3-0 Mönchengladbach, Mainz 0-0 Paderborn, Elversberg 3-2 Leverkusen, Cologne 3-2 Hoffenheim, Dortmund 2-0 Hamburg, Freiburg 4-1 Werder Bremen, Augsburg 3-0 Schalke Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Talking points

Bayern’s opening night brutality had been, as so often in the past, aided and abetted by their visitors Stuttgart, who tend to play in their normal front-foot style against the champions and are accordingly ripped to shreds even in games (like this one) in which they have good spells. Michael Olise was on the scoresheet but Harry Kane didn’t even need to score, while Ismaël Saibari offered enterprise and two assists from the bench. Vincent Kompany’s team are frightening.

View image in fullscreen Michael Olise scores for Bayern Munich. Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/Reuters

Still, Dortmund had taken hope from their second half in last week’s Super Cup and were very attractive in a one-sided first half against Hamburg, a departure from previous Niko Kovac teams. But although they cruised to a 2-0 win there was a huge blow, with new boy Giannis Konstantelias rupturing his ACL on his full debut, minutes after scoring the second. BVB now have to consider free agent replacements, with both Jadon Sancho and Reiss Nelson among the names circulating.

Saïd El Mala, who nearly ended up at BVB, instead wore the FC Köln No 10 shirt for the first time and helped to inspire a comeback win against Hoffenheim, scoring a first equaliser before new signing Thijs Dallinga struck two memorable goals in a 3-2 victory.

Elversberg’s aforementioned former star Ebnoutalib had an explosive start to the campaign, hitting a hat-trick at Union Berlin. It was an afternoon of vindication for the Moroccan striker, who scored on his Frankfurt debut against Dortmund in January and was then injured shortly after. “It’s good for my mind,” Ebnoutalib said after the game, even though an injury-time Tim Skarke equaliser snared Union a point after they had trailed 3-1 (and debutant Eintracht goalkeeper Noah Atubolu had needed to perform excellently to keep them at bay that long).

Schalke’s return to the top flight started brightly at Augsburg, with Finn Dahmen keeping them at bay in the early stages before Michael Gregoritsch punctured his former club’s hopes with the opener, and it was virtually one-way traffic from there, ending with 10 men and a 3-0 loss. Still, they could be Werder Bremen, given a 4-1 Sunday kicking at Freiburg the day after their star man Jens Stage was confirmed as out injured until the new year.

Sports.title: Chelsea’s perfect yet unserious start to the Premier League season | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Two Premier League games played for Chelsea under Xabi Alonso: two wins and seven goals scored. It’s the sort of start that would delight many new managers – only two other clubs can boast about a six-point start this Premier League season (albeit with Arsenal to play later on Monday). Points gained in this odd transitional phase, when almost nobody seems quite ready, could prove extremely valuable come the end of the season. And yet, for all the attacking potency, there must also be concerns about Chelsea’s openness and the five goals conceded.

Context must also be considered, and it projects both ways. It’s early in the season. There has been, as ever, a lot of change at Chelsea. They will get better; they will achieve greater coherence. But equally there has to be a sense of realism about the nature of the teams they’ve played. Brighton may have thrashed a shambolic Aston Villa 4-0 last weekend, but they were missing seven frontline players at Stamford Bridge and still put three past Chelsea on Sunday. And while Fulham looked very lively as Chelsea won 3-2 on the opening weekend, they couldn’t muster a shot on target against Sunderland on Sunday.

How good are Brighton? Were Villa just terrible on that first weekend? Was it really just Granit Xhaka’s appeal for Sunderland to be themselves again that made a side that had lost at Ipswich capable of dominating Fulham through midfield? It’s very hard at this stage to trace any patterns, other than perhaps to say that Xhaka’s performance against Fulham showed why Chelsea wanted to sign him in the summer.

The systems are different, so the comparison perhaps isn’t entirely fair, but Xhaka, and his midfield partner Noah Sadiki, offered a level of control that Chelsea under Alonso have so far been entirely lacking – striking, given the degree of control Enzo Maresca insisted upon as manager last season. Both Chelsea games so far have felt almost like a pastiche of the modern Bundesliga: all high tempo and turnovers, chaotic and fun and slightly unserious.

This is not how it’s meant to be. Alonso’s Bayer Leverkusen side, in which Xhaka was partnered in central midfield by one of Robert Andrich, Aleix García, or Exequiel Palacios, won the Bundesliga in 2024 conceding only 24 goals in 34 league games. They averaged 59.5% possession, whereas Chelsea so far this season have had just 32%. Perhaps when Moisés Caicedo returns to fitness – he managed 14 minutes from the bench on Sunday before being forced off again – his energy and mobility will bring an immediate improvement, but the way both Fulham and Brighton have at times sliced through Chelsea suggests there are structural issues.

The usual criticism of the 3-4-2-1 formation used by Chelsea is that it is too blockish, that creativity comes almost entirely from the two inside-forwards, making the side playing it predictable if they dominate possession. Its usage, at least in the Premier League, tends to have been as a counterattacking system – this is how, for instance, Oliver Glasner deployed it at Crystal Palace over the last two seasons. Two holding players operating in front of a back three should provide the trapezoid shape that has become the default for sides hoping to guard against the counter. Yet with Roméo Lavia alongside either Reece James or Malo Gusto, that solidity has been lacking.

Why, then, is Alonso’s system suffering the opposite problem? The issue really stems from a positive: Alonso’s 3-4-2-1 is not the blockish formation often seen. Rather it is a basis from which multiple variations stem. It has a variety that helps overcome a potential over-reliance on the two inside-forwards. That’s how, for instance, center back Maxence Lacroix ended up bursting through to set up a goal against Fulham. Breaking the lines and varying the pattern is part of the pattern.

The defensive concerns predate Alonso. It’s been 18 games since Chelsea last kept a clean sheet, their longest run in the top flight since 1961. While the signing of Emí Martínez should give them a more assertive, less error-prone figure in goal than Robert Sánchez in goal, there will be issues, at least in the short term, in getting the balance right at full-back. Plus, defences are best when they are stable, when interactions become automatic; while Lacroix is the sort of central defender Chelsea have been short of and will almost certainly make them better in the long term, and while Josh Acheampong, who played well against Fulham and came off the bench against Brighton, looks a hugely promising presence (he started only eight league games last season); incorporating both of them while adapting to a new goalkeeper will take time. There is a cost to the constant churn at Chelsea.

Arsenal, next Sunday, will provide a far stiffer test. Chelsea’s front three of João Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer give them a puncher’s chance, but there is a chance Arsenal render them irrelevant by dominating the game through the midfield. They are two teams at very different stages of their development.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
Sports.content:
1 Calming influence at Old Trafford

Amid the concerns at Manchester United, one player unquestioned is Senne Lammens. The goalkeeper produced some important first-half saves against Ipswich to keep his side in the game in difficult circumstances. A relaxed character, the Belgian is a calming influence in an emotional environment, especially with a panicked defence. When Julio Enciso was through on goal, Lammens had to decide when to come and how far, getting his distance and angles perfect to ensure the Paraguay attacker was repelled. His distribution was also excellent, instigating rapid attacks and bringing the dynamism demanded from the modern goalkeeper. Will Unwin

View image in fullscreen Senne Lammens directs his defence during a wet afternoon at Old Trafford. Photograph: Colorsport/Alan Martin/Shutterstock

2 Liverpool’s curious transfer strategy

Oliver Glasner said he would celebrate the closure of the transfer window with a pint on Wednesday night. Andoni Iraola would surely be tempted to join his Nottingham Forest counterpart – perhaps in Ye Olde Trip to Jerusalem – were it not for the distance between them. It underlines the strangeness of Liverpool’s recent transfer strategy that the understandable excitement generated by Bradley Barcola’s impending £123m arrival from Paris Saint-Germain is offset by concern over the gaps in Iraola’s squad that have not been filled – right-wing, right-back and central midfield being the most obvious ones. The need to improve in all three departments was evident as Liverpool had to fight back to salvage a late 2-2 draw for the second Premier League game in succession. “We don’t know what the squad is going to be on 2 September,” said Iraola, surely holding out hope that wingers are not the only incomings before Tuesday. “I think every analysis I can make is when I know and when everything finishes, when I will know who is going to be here all the season or until January.” Andy Hunter

3 Alonso brushes off need to keep the ball

Chelsea prioritised control under Enzo Maresca but they have been counterattacking under Xabi Alonso. They have had little of the ball during the Spaniard’s first two league games. Chelsea had 38.1% possession during last week’s win over Fulham and 25% when they beat Brighton on Sunday, although Alonso insists this is not a strategy. “You need context to data,” he said after the Brighton game. “After 30 minutes we have scored [to make it] 3-0. Probably, in that moment, we have played too much with the result, instead of keep playing. But it is never that approach, I don’t say today we need to have 60% or 20%.” Jacob Steinberg

View image in fullscreen Cole Palmer celebrates scoring with Morgan Rogers. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

4 Armstrong saga sets out battle lines

Deciding not to sell Harrison Armstrong will quell unrest at Everton for now but perhaps not for long. Factions are apparent. David Moyes has been on the defensive since the chief executive, Angus Kinnear, said the Friedkin ownership group saw last season as a “failure”. Moyes aligned himself with those fans at Bournemouth threatening to protest should Armstrong be sold to Nottingham Forest. Selling a local boy for “pure profit” was beyond the pale. “I’d say the manager’s an Evertonian,” Moyes said. “Supporters aren’t always wrong.” His harking back to harmonious working relationships at Preston and his initial spell at Everton was pointed. A manager who faced criticism as Everton slumped in the closing months of the season threw it back to his employers. “I have said we could do with strengthening,” he said, after a performance where the lack of a proper right-back was apparent. The remainder of the transfer window, in which Everton have little wriggle room, may deepen battle lines. John Brewin

View image in fullscreen Harrison Armstrong applauds the fans who sang for him all match. Photograph: Matt Impey/Shutterstock

5 Jaissle bedding in swiftly at Newcastle

Matthias Jaissle laughed when asked if he felt a responsibility to develop players who had signed for the club before he had. “The job of the coach is to get the best out of your players,” the Newcastle manager replied. With all the focus before Saturday’s game on summer spends and squads in transition, Jaissle built victory over Spurs with revitalised performances from players written off after poor seasons. Yoane Wissa led the line with ferocious energy, Anthony Elanga took his chance coolly to open the scoring. There was also an energetic showing from Joe Willock, and even an assist for the maligned Nick Woltemade. New signings were impressive too – notably Nico González and his range of passing – with more to be bedded in still. But Jaissle has shown he can build a team from the parts available, an achievement that can make victories feel all the more sweeter. It is notable that the Toon Army seem very much onboard with their German head coach already. Paul MacInnes

Allow Instagram content? This article includes content provided by Instagram . We ask for your permission before anything is loaded, as they may be using cookies and other technologies. To view this content, click 'Allow and continue'. Allow and continue

6 Hull keep playing to their strengths

Two games, two wins, two clean sheets: what is the secret ingredient in Hull’s winning formula? They have an eclectic squad and Sergej Jakirovic wants to add at least a right-back and another goalkeeper before Tuesday’s transfer deadline. Jakirovic said his head was exploding due to the hectic window and joked his proposed new three-year contract remains unsigned because the ink in his office has run dry owing to 13 summer arrivals. At Coventry on Saturday, Hull registered fewer shots than Frank Lampard’s side and fewer touches in the opposition 18-yard box, and made 182 passes to their opponent’s 501. Liam Millar’s winner was courtesy of a superb counterattack and Hull undeniably played to their strengths. “We prefer letting the other team have the ball and just defending,” said the striker Oli McBurnie. “We’ve seen teams dominate the ball in the Championship, come into the Premier League and try to use the same style and it’s really, really difficult. It’s not all about looking pretty and having a million passes.” Ben Fisher

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

7 Unsettled Palace await crunch week

Crystal Palace are in a tricky spot. Daniel Muñoz looks ready to join Nottingham Forest, Galatasaray want Ismaïla Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta is injured. Sarr and Mateta, a duo responsible for the large bulk of Palace’s goals last season, missed the defeat by Manchester City and their absence was felt in attack. Eddie Nketiah was wasteful and Jørgen Strand Larsen was ineffective. Pierre Sage, beaten in his first two games after replacing Oliver Glasner as manager, could do with reinforcements arriving before the window shuts. Axel Disasi should make a difference once he slots into a defence weakened by Maxence Lacroix’s departure, but it has been a worrying start for Palace. JS

8 Farke’s nous can match Leeds’ ambition

Premier League managers rarely get the acclaim when things are going well but on Sunday afternoon, it felt right to shine a deserved spotlight on Leeds’ manager, Daniel Farke, after they continued their unbeaten start to the season. Farke’s decision to revert to a back five last November against Manchester City was a turning point in Leeds’ season and his own time in charge. It is not an exaggeration to suggest Farke was under extreme pressure at that stage, but his show of flexibility ultimately saved his job. He showed that tactical flexibility again on Sunday. Leeds were outplayed by Brentford in the first half before Farke switched from a five to a four at the back. The result was a much better second-half showing, a deserved equaliser from Dominic Calvert-Lewin and a point Leeds were good value for. Leeds are a hugely ambitious club, and that ambition may rear its head again before the window shuts on Tuesday. The early evidence appears to be they have a manager who can match that ambition. Aaron Bower

View image in fullscreen Daniel Farke’s tactical change helped spur Leeds on to score an equaliser via Dominic Calvert-Lewin. Photograph: Jason Cairnduff/Action Images/Reuters

9 Mukiele proving to be Black Cats’ bargain

Football – like life – is full of mysteries. How, for instance, did Sunderland end up paying only £12m to sign Nordi Mukiele from Paris Saint-Germain last summer? And how has the 28-year-old right-back or centre-half – who spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Bayer Leverkusen – won only one France cap? Mukiele was deployed in central defense as Sunderland beat Fulham 1-0 at the Stadium of Light on Sunday and he proved absolutely outstanding, making a couple of goal-preventing blocks. Álvaro Arbeloa was left thoroughly dejected after suffering two defeats in his first two matches as a Premier League manager. “I was really impressed with Nordi and I told him this,” said Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager. “Nordi showed us today that he’s a great player.” Sunday’s man of the match ranks as one of the biggest Premier League bargain signings of recent years. Louise Taylor

10 Davis’s form could catch Tuchel’s eye

Considering the general dearth when it comes to English left-backs, Ipswich’s Leif Davis has spent a long time under the radar. Back in the Premier League and facing some of the world’s best opponents, the full-back looks stylish in both directions. He is competent in defence, diligently holding his position and giving wingers a difficult time but can also push forward, proved by his opener at Old Trafford, in addition to an array of fine passing, long and short. If Thomas Tuchel is short of options over the course of this season, Davis could and should become more prominent in his thoughts if his form continues. WU

Sports.title: Watkins faces Toney clash as strikers push for Saudi supremacy and Tuchel’s attention
Sports.content:
Ollie Watkins and Ivan Toney spent 33 minutes on the pitch together a few weeks ago in Miami as England beat France 6-4 in a game for third place at the World Cup. They will be reunited on Tuesday in Riyadh for Al-Hilal v Al-Ahli, the first big clash between title hopefuls in the Saudi Pro League season.

Aston Villa fans will be hoping that, starting against Arsenal on Monday, Nicolas Jackson can quickly help them forget their departed talisman. That’s what Toney did at Brentford back in 2020 when he replaced Watkins. It may not only be supporters in the West Midlands and west London who will be curious to see how their alumni get on in west Asia. England’s heach coach, Thomas Tuchel, will surely tune in (or even turn up?) to get a look at the two forwards battling to become the clear understudy to Harry Kane as a new international cycle starts.

Before that bronze-medal match, Watkins and Toney had enough time together in North America on and off the bench to chat about Saudi Arabia. The former has joined Al-Hilal and probably doesn’t need any advice on how to score goals in the Saudi Pro League but if he does then his Three Lions teammate is the man to ask.

Toney arrived in the Middle East two years ago, signing for Al-Ahli in Jeddah, the country’s most passionate football city, to play under Matthias Jaissle. He took a little time to get going in his first season but ended with 23 league goals and the Asian Champions League title, the club’s first. The second brought 32 league goals and Toney was pipped to the Golden Boot by Julián Quiñones on the final day but there was the small consolation of a second Asian triumph. With four goals in three games this season, more honours, of a personal and team nature, are on the cards.

Al-Ahli have won one domestic league title in more than 40 years and that is their focus this season but Watkins joins a historically winning machine with record hauls at home and in Asia – 19 and four respectively. Even before the big spending started in the summer of 2023, Al-Hilal were an institution and could make a case for being the biggest in Asia, with social media followings that ranked alongside any in the world. Finishing second, as they did last season, is not tolerated for long and there has been plenty of criticism of the coach, Simone Inzaghi, for allowing their local rivals Al-Nassr, for whom Cristiano Ronaldo plays, to win last season.

Watkins’ timing off the pitch looks as good as that on it. He is joining a team that appear to be approaching top gear, scoring nine goals in their first two league games. With service from Rúben Neves, Sergej Milinkovic-Savic, Crysencio Summerville and, potentially, Gabriel Martinelli, the forward should hit the ground running. Well, not too much running. The temperatures are in the mid-forties during the day in Riyadh, and it is hard to overstate how much of a shock it can be at first, but the mercury will soon start to drop to more manageable levels.

Saudi spending has also dropped since that summer of 2023 when SPL clubs splashed out more than £700m on players such as Karim Benzema (who is poised to leave Al-Hilal), N’Golo Kanté, Riyad Mahrez, Roberto Firmino, Sadio Mané and others with the experience to go with their star power. The focus since has switched to younger and cheaper options who offer resale value.

Théo Hernandez at Al-Hilal came in 2025 for not much more than £20m. The teenage striker Mohamed Kader Meïté came from Rennes for not much more and the 18-year-old Côte d’Ivoire Under-23 international has opened his account for the season.

View image in fullscreen Ivan Toney scores for Al Ahli this month. He got 32 league goals last season. Photograph: Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images

Watkins, at 30, is a bit different. It shows there is money available for the right stars and, given the bewildering sums flying around the Premier League, the reported fee of just over £50m does not seem especially excessive. Al-Hilal’s transfer dealings are, perhaps, slightly different from those of the other top teams. The Blues were part of the Big Four taken over by the Public Investment Fund in 2023 but were handed over to the billionaire businessman Prince Al Waleed bin Talal this year.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Ivan Toney and Ollie Watkins will hope to be part of the England picked next month for Nations League fixtures. Photograph: Eddie Keogh/The FA/Getty Images

Al-Hilal’s spending has outstripped the others’ in this window and the pressure is on. Watkins is used to Villa, a second-level Premier League team unable to challenge for the title, a situation reinforced over the past few weeks as the Europa League winners have sold players. Now he is at a club that demands success, the epitome of Asia’s establishment.

Al-Ahli, helped by Ivan Toney, are of the same stature. Another, more personal, prize may be up for grabs in the international arena and Tuesday night in Riyadh is an opportunity for Watkins and Toney to grab English – and German – attention.

Sports.title: Wrexham attempt to sign Championship star from rival in manic end to transfer window
Sports.content:
Wrexham attempt to sign Championship star from rival in manic end to transfer window

Wrexham are pursuing Sheffield United attacking midfielder Callum O'Hare, talkSPORT understands.

Talks are ongoing with the Blades ahead of a busy final 24 hours of the transfer window for the Welsh outfit.

4 O'Hare has scored twice in five games in all competitions for Sheffield United this term

Business looming

With O'Hare potentially set to join a Championship rival of the Blades, he could be one of four arrivals at the Racecourse Ground ahead of Deadline Day.

Joe Worrall is formalising his £2m move from Burnley, as talkSPORT exclusively revealed on Sunday.

Wrexham are also looking to strengthen their forward line, having seen approaches turned down for Ipswich striker Anis Mehmeti and Millwall's Femi Azeez.

However, both players are understood to be holding out for different moves.

talkSPORT can exclusively reveal Brighton have had a £10m bid rejected for Azeez, who fired in 11 league goals last term.

As well as Wrexham, Mehmeti is reportedly attracting interest from Birmingham City and Derby.

The Red Dragons could also be set for some departures before Tuesday's 11pm deadline, with ex-Wolves captain Conor Coady recently having his contract terminated by mutual consent.

Meanwhile, Birmingham are showing interest in Wrexham midfielder Josh Windass.

However, it is unclear whether talks will progress between now and the end of the window, with last season's top scorer revealing to talkSPORT his plans to stay in North Wales earlier this summer.

Callum O'Hare's career

With Wrexham set for a busy end to the summer transfer window, O'Hare would certainly be the standout arrival if they are able to secure his signature.

4 Phil Parkinson is adding some extra defensive steel to his team Credit: Getty

4 As well as targeting playmaker O'Hare, Worrall is poised to join Wrexham from Burnley Credit: Getty

The Aston Villa academy graduate boasts a wealth of Championship experience, having spent the last five years in the second tier - first with Coventry City and now Sheffield United.

He has made 225 league appearances for the two clubs, scoring 25 goals and assisting 37 times.

O'Hare joined Sheffield United in 2024, and has since established himself as a key player for them.

During his time at Bramall Lane he has featured 98 times altogether, chipping in with 14 goals and 14 assists.

The 28-year-old has started all three of Sheffield United's Championship games this season.

He got on the scoresheet in their last match - a 2-2 draw with Cardiff, which saw the Blades take a point from their third straight game.

4 O'Hare first cut his teeth in the Championship during his four-year stay at Coventry between 2020 and 2024 Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, Wrexham's late push to sign O'Hare comes as they look to strengthen following a disappointing start to the season.

After missing out on the Championship play-off places on the final day of last season, the Welsh outfit are looking to go one further and continue their remarkable rise up the English football pyramid.

However, Parkinson's side are currently winless after their first three league games, drawing twice before suffering a 2-1 defeat to Birmingham in their last outing.

Wrexham currently sit 20th on two points, but have 43 games left of the season to transform their fortunes.

Sports.title: Wrexham rip up player’s contract after playing just six games for club
Sports.content:
Wrexham rip up player’s contract after playing just six games for club

Conor Coady has become a free agent following his departure from Wrexham, the club have confirmed.

The ex-England international joined the Welsh outfit from Leicester last summer in a £2million deal, penning a two-year contract.

3 Coady signed a two-year contract with Wrexham last summer Credit: Getty

But Coady has struggled for game time since then, making just six appearances in all competitions for the club.

He spent the second half of the season on loan at Charlton and featured 12 times as the Addicks secured Championship safety.

The centre-back later then to Wrexham for the new season, but was

Coady hasn't been included in the matchday squad for all four of the Hollywood-owned outfit's games so far this term.

And his time in north Wales has now come to a premature end, with the club announcing the news on social media.

End of the road

In a post on X, Wrexham wrote: "We can confirm that Conor Coady has left the Club following the mutual termination of his contract.

"We wish Conor all the best for the future."

No further details were given on where the former Wolves captain could go next, although Welsh rivals Swansea have previously been credited with an interest.

An early departure from the Racecourse Ground is a far from ideal scenario for Coady, who admitted earlier this summer he hadn't given up hope of a revival at Wrexham.

Having joined the Red Dragons ahead of their return to the Championship following a third consecutive promotion, he moved to Phil Parkinson's side with the Premier League in his sights.

3 Coady's two-year contract at Wrexham included the option of a further year, but this was not exercised Credit: Getty

Speaking in May, Coady said: "When I went there last summer, it was something I really wanted to be a part of and sometimes I think people look at footballers and think something's happened.

"Nothing's ever personal in football. Sometimes a manager just doesn't take to you and I think that was what it was.

"[But] I've got a really good relationship with Phil Parkinson - nothing's ever happened between us.

"I had a great relationship when I was there and they were brilliant with me in January when it came to maybe wanting to leave if there was an opportunity.

"Wrexham is a brilliant, brilliant club so I can't sit here now and rule anything out because I don't know what's going to happen."

Conor Coady's career

With Coady now a free agent, there will no doubt be plenty of clubs keen to take on a player with his wealth of experience.

3 Coady is best known for his seven-year spell at Wolves Credit: Getty

The 33-year-old has made 198 Premier League appearances and captained Wolves in the top flight.

He skippered the West Midlands side to promotion from the Championship in 2018 and held onto the armband.

Coady also has almost 200 Championship appearances to his name, having joined Huddersfield on a permanent deal in 2014 after starting his senior career at Liverpool.

He then made the switch to Wolves, where he went on to play over 300 games for the club across an eight-year spell, earning 10 senior England caps during this time too.

His time at the club came to an end in 2023, as he fell out of favour and secured a loan switch to Everton.

Coady then left permanently a year later to join Leicester, where he helped the Foxes win the Championship title.

But following their immediate relegation from the Premier League in 2025 he made the move to Wrexham.

Sports.title: ‘Unicorn’ – Newcastle United agree £55m deal to sign next Romelu Lukaku
Sports.content:
Newcastle United have agreed a fee for Lille forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo, talkSPORT understands.

The Magpies are set to pay an initial £51m and an additional £4m for the versatile attacker.

3 Fernandez-Pardo has been linked with clubs all around Europe, but he has picked Newcastle Credit: AFP

The 21-year-old is now set to fly to Tyneside to complete a medical and sign a five-year deal.

Newcastle have chased the Belgian international all summer, but the interest has only just been revived, and he will become the latest senior signing for Matthias Jaissle.

It is a deal that will likely see club record signing Nick Woltemade depart.

Juventus are advancing in talks to sign the German international on loan for the season with an option to buy.

But Fernandez-Pardo is a player who European football expert Andy Brassell is a huge fan of.

Speaking to talkSPORT.com earlier this year, he said: “I love Fernandez-Pardo.

“He’s kind of a unicorn. It’s taken a long time to work out exactly what he is – I think not just for us but for him as well.

“People looked at him and thought, ‘He’s a winger’, but he’s really flourishing as a centre-forward.

"I think people’s understanding of what a centre-forward can be and should be has changed a little bit. Sometimes we think that a centre-forward does have to be someone who’s six-foot plus, who can put themselves about.

“But I think it’s really notable that since Lille’s form has improved towards the end of the season, they were unbeaten in 13…”

3 Jaissle is receiving the backing he would have wanted in the transfer market Credit: Getty

And Brassell believes that the 6ft1 forward is the long-term Romelu Lukaku replacement for Belgium.

He said: “Fernandez-Pardo has all of the winger’s skillset in that he’s very, very good in tight spaces. He’s a good dribbler; he’s good at beating players; he’s quick.

“But…they’ve allowed [recently departed Lille boss] Bruno Genesio, who’s an exceptional coach and an exceptional developer of young players…to use those traditional winger’s skills in a more central area.

“I think this is maybe the future for Belgium in terms of a striker [to replace Romelu Lukaku]."

The forward scored eight goals in Ligue 1 last season to help his club finish third and in the Champions League.

3 Fernandez-Pardo is seen as the next striker for Belgium Credit: Getty

Newcastle's transfer window

Once Fernandez-Pardo joins, Newcastle would have made eight senior signings this summer.

It will also take their spending towards £300m, but due to the sales of Sandro Tonali, Anthony Gordon and Bruno Guimaraes, the net spend will still be very low.

Nottingham Forest are also interested in Jacob Murphy, which could see the Toon make another signing as well if the long-serving winger departs.

But since Jaissle has arrived, Amar Dedic, Nico Gonzalez and now Fernandez-Pardo would have followed him to Tyneside.

The Magpies have also made a strong start to the season with four points from six and progress in the Carabao Cup.

As long as the deal progresses smoothly, you will be able to hear Fernandez-Pardo's debut on Saturday live and exclusively on talkSPORT as Newcastle welcome Bournemouth.

Sports.title: Bizarre reason why Bradley Barcola has taken rogue Liverpool shirt number
Sports.content:
Bizarre reason why Bradley Barcola has taken rogue Liverpool shirt number

Liverpool has confirmed that Bradley Barcola has inherited his unusual shirt number at the club, and it's down to his love of FIFA.

The Reds have confirmed the signing of the Frenchman from Paris Saint-Germain for an initial £106million, rising to £123m.



3 Barcola wears 29 at PSG, and that number is what he will now wear at Liverpool Credit: Getty

Barcola has always been their number one target this summer, and Liverpool have finally landed their man.

What shirt number will Barcola take?

There were a few options for the France forward when he officially joins Liverpool.

The obvious choice would be Mohamed Salah’s 11, which is still free after he left to join Turkish Super Lig club Trabzonspor this summer.



Aside from that, 16, 17, 24, 26, 27, 29 are all available.

That 29 shirt has now been confirmed as the one he has opted for, however, due to its association with FIFA, now called EA FC.

It is the number worn by fictional character Alex Hunter in 'The Journey' series in the game.



Barcola has previously said: “When I was younger, I used to play FIFA. In the story mode with Alex Hunter, this number became symbolic for me.

"I thought to myself: ‘The day I go pro, it’ll be number 29.’ And here I am, I adopted it, and now I’ll never let it go.”



He adopted that number at PSG and has followed suit at Liverpool.

3 Barcola is only the 10th player in Liverpool history to wear the No.29 shirt Credit: Getty

The last person to wear 29 for Liverpool was Arthur Melo in the 2022/23 season.

Dominic Solanke, Fabio Borini, Krisztián Németh, Gabriel Paletta, Patrice Luzi, Stephen Wright, Brad Friedel, and David Thompson are the other players to have worn the digits at Anfield.

talkSPORT verdict

Former Crystal Palace owner Simon Jordan believes Barcola will be a good signing for Liverpool with wingers playing greater importance in today’s game.



He told White and Jordan: “He's a good player. He will be a good player for Liverpool. I don't think it has the same connotations as Isak.

“It goes to the point of what Jimmy Floyd Hasselbaink was making yesterday about how important wingers are and how the game has moved into wide players.

“We saw it years ago when Real Madrid came over and bought Laurie Cunningham from West Bromwich Albion.

“Wingers were a fundamental part of it. It's a part of the English game that was sort of phased out after Alf Ramsey for a period of time.



3 Barcola is already a double Champions League winner with PSG Credit: Getty

“Now it's back in vogue and wingers and forward players of that nature are so pivotal to teams, if they can work hard and add value as well as going forward.

“He's a young 23-year-old player that I think could be a roaring success.”

Sports.title: The five Tottenham players expected to leave in mass exodus before deadline slams shut
Sports.content:
The five Tottenham players expected to leave in mass exodus before deadline slams shut

Tottenham Hotspur's departure lounge is shaping up to be one of the busiest ahead of deadline day.

Spurs have a burning need to trim the squad following a hectic and expensive summer, with eight new faces joining the club.



4 Tonali became Spurs' club-record signing when he joined for £100m Credit: Getty

That number may rise to nine after Spurs agreed a deal in principle with Everton to sign Iliman Ndiaye.

Despite the vast expenditure, which has seen the club break their transfer record twice, Roberto De Zerbi's side are yet to get off the mark in the Premier League.

But Spurs' fortunes may change once De Zerbi knows which players he will be able to call upon, at least until January.



So, who is on the chopping block in north London?

Richarlison

Richarlison was one of three players namechecked by De Zerbi during his post-match press conference following the Newcastle loss who expressed a desire to move on.

In terms of where the Brazilian would go, talkSPORT understands Spurs are in advanced talks with Everton over the forward.



The deal would be separate to the one sending Ndiaye the opposite way.

Richarlison made over 150 appearances for the Toffees before joining Spurs in July 2022 for £60million.



Pape Matar Sarr

Pape Matar Sarr is another member of the trio who told De Zerbi he wants to leave Spurs.

And, similarly to Richarlison, it appears the midfielder's wish will be granted as talkSPORT understands Juventus will sign Sarr on loan with an obligation to buy.

4 Sarr is yet to feature for Spurs this season as he recovers from a small injury Credit: Getty

Once complete, Sarr will reunite with Guglielmo Vicario, who moved from Spurs to Juventus on a season-long loan.



Sarr sought a move having fallen down the midfield pecking order at Spurs following the arrivals of Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes.

Kevin Danso

The third and final member who told De Zerbi they wanted out, Kevin Danso finds himself in a similar scenario to Sarr as a result of Spurs' summer business.

Despite starting six of Spurs' final seven games last term to help the club stay up, Danso's chances of game time have drastically reduced after Jan Paul van Hecke and Marcos Senesi joined.

In terms of where Danso will end up, talkSPORT understands Spurs and Sunderland are in discussions over the Austrian, who would move on a permanent deal.



Danso has already agreed personal terms with the Black Cats, who will compete in this season's Europa League.

4 Danso first moved to Spurs on loan in February last year before he was signed permanently Credit: Getty

Mikey Moore

Another player who is set to be squeezed out due to Spurs' summer business is Mikey Moore.

The 19-year-old has started two of the club's three competitive fixtures this term, but that appears to be as much action as he'll see for the north London outfit.



That's because talkSPORT understands Moore is set to join German club Koln on loan.

It will be Moore's second loan spell in as many seasons, having spent the 2025/26 campaign with Rangers.

Koln enjoyed a winning start to the Bundesliga campaign, coming from behind to beat Hoffenheim 3-2 in their season opener.

4 Moore featured heavily for Spurs during their pre-season Credit: Getty



Souza

Souza has rarely got a look-in since he joined Spurs in January.

The Brazilian made just four appearances for the club in the second half of last term, two of which were starts.

But he's set to get valuable experience elsewhere as multiple reports state Souza will link up with Porto for the 26/27 season.

He'll then return to Spurs next summer.

Sports.title: Liverpool nearly break British transfer record with confirmation of Bradley Barcola
Sports.content:
Liverpool nearly break British transfer record with confirmation of Bradley Barcola

Liverpool have confirmed the signing of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain for an initial £106million, rising to £123m.

It is the second-most expensive signing in Premier League history, with Alexander Isak's move to Anfield last year, the only deal ahead of it.



5 Barcola looks set to depart Paris Saint-Germain this summer Credit: Getty

5 Barcola's transfer is the third over £100million this summer by Premier League clubs

Liverpool haven't confirmed how long his contract is, but it is a long-term deal for the winger.

Speaking to the club's website, Barcola said: It's a great pride to be able to play for Liverpool. I'm very happy.



"It took a long time but I'm really happy today to be able to play for Liverpool and all I want is to be on the pitch and be able to play.

"I hope to achieve very big things. First of all, winning the Premier League – it's one of my biggest dreams in my life.



"It is to do that and to stay in this team in the long term – that's why I signed a long contract – and I hope I can do it."

Barcola will wear the number 29 shirt due to his love of FIFA and Alex Hunter, who was a character in the career mode of the game.



How the deal played out

PSG wanted to get a fee worth more than those paid for Morgan Rogers (£117m) and Elliot Anderson (£116m) this summer.

PSG were also determined to get more for Barcola than the €140m package that saw Yan Diomande move to Real Madrid.

It's also understood Liverpool will cover PSG's solidarity payment to Lyon, thought to be around £5m.

As talkSPORT previously reported, Liverpool made it clear they were not willing to break their own Premier League transfer record having spent £125m on Alexander Isak one year ago.



The French international has wanted the move to Anfield all summer, rejecting interest from others to

Barcola was essentially made surplus to requirements by PSG after several attacking players arrived.

The Champions League holders have recruited Ferran Torres from Barcelona.

Mika Godts and Maghnes Akliouche have also arrived in the French capital.



The Reds are still looking to recruit a right winger as well.

They have seen two offers for Yankuba Minteh turned down, with them moving on for Ismailia Sarr.

5 Barcola has his move to Anfield, where he will be a key player Credit: Getty

There were reports of an offer from Andoni Iraola's side for the Senegalese international, but Liverpool sources have told talkSPORT that isn't the case.

However, Sarr is now pushing to make the move happen before the deadline.



End of a long chase

Barcola emerged as Liverpool's top target for the left wing position at the start of the summer.

There was fleeting interest from Arsenal, but the Gunners never pursued it further.

That left Liverpool with a free run at Barcola, though the deal isn't done until he's put pen to paper.

talkSPORT initially reported that PSG wanted £145million for Barcola.

Liverpool were never prepared to pay that, so there has been some compromise on the fee.



5 Spurs would like to add Gakpo to Savio and Omar Marmoush Credit: Getty

Transfer dominoes

Barcola's arrival and the pursuit of another winger is important for Cody Gakpo's future.

The Dutchman scored in the 2-2 draw against Newcastle United on Sunday.

But with Barcola, Iraola will have Victor Munoz and Rio Ngumoha as options on the left.



talkSPORT understands that Tottenham Hotspur are still keen on the forward.

But Manchester City lead the race, with the player choosing to join City.

Spurs have signed Savio from Man City in a deal worth up to £85million, while Omar Marmoush has joined on loan with an obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

But Gakpo will only swap clubs if Liverpool land another winger.

5 Andoni Iraola is about to be handed a major boost with the addition of Barcola Credit: Getty



Got their man

Iraola made it clear ahead of the season that Liverpool were fully expecting to sign a winger.

The fact Ngumoha was at right wing against Newcastle highlighted their problem.

Speaking about that situation during pre-season, Iraola said: "There are obvious situations that we know where we need to sign players. A winger, for example – we definitely need to sign a winger.

"But there are other situations that we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what’s the cost, how we also see the players we have.



"We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust but it is still not the ideal situation.

"So, it will depend on a lot of things."

Sports.title: Liverpool set to sign £30m ‘next Thibaut Courtois’ – what this means for Giorgi Mamardashvili
Sports.content:
Liverpool set to sign £30m ‘next Thibaut Courtois’ – what this means for Giorgi Mamardashvili

Liverpool have reached an agreement with Genk to sign 18-year-old goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans, talkSPORT understands.

The young Belgian is set to join the Reds in a package deal worth worth €35million (£29.9m).

4 Iraola is set to strengthen his goalkeeping department Credit: Getty

Brughmans, who has been described as the next Thiabut Courtois, is expected to undergo a medical immediately, ahead of completing a permanent move to Anfield in the summer of 2027.

Liverpool goalkeepers

This move could come in the nick of time for Liverpool, with No.1 Alisson's current contract expiring at the end of the season.

With the Brazilian looking likely to depart, Giorgi Mamardashvili has long been primed as his successor.

The Georgian finally moved to Merseyside ahead of the 2025/26 campaign, having been announced by the club a year earlier.

He deputised in Alisson's absence last term, featuring in 19 games in all competitions - nine of which came in the Premier League, where he kept two clean sheets.

But Brughmans' expected arrival next summer has now cast doubt over whether Mamardashvili is the long-term solution between the sticks.

Having failed to convince with his performances when deputising for Alisson, Liverpool now appear to be considering other options.

With Brughmans set to join next summer, their succession plan looks to have change, and Mamardashvili may well even decide his future lies elsewhere.

According to Marca journalist Matteo Moretto, the 25-year-old is drawing interest from Premier League rivals Nottingham Forest.

Though those links have been played down to talkSPORT and Mamardashvili is set to remain at Anfield this season to be No.2.

4 Giorgi Mamardashvili's path to the No.1 shirt at Liverpool could be impacted by Brughmans' arrival Credit: Getty

4 Alisson is into the final year of his Liverpool contract, having triggered a 12-month extension in March Credit: Getty

Meanwhile, if the Georgia international stays at Anfield long-term, he is now likely to face a real fight for the No.1 spot from Brughmans.

Who is Lucca Brughman?

The Liverpool-boundBelgium youth international has earned a reputation as one of the most promising emerging goalkeepers.

Brughmans is a graduate of Genk's youth system - the same academy which has produced Thibaut Courtois and Chelsea's Mike Penders.

The teenager made his professional debut for Jong Genk - the club’s reserve side - aged 16 in 2024, and went on to make 32 appearances for them in Belgium's second-tier Challenger Pro League.

Last season, he stepped up to the first team and started all 10 of their Pro League play-off fixtures.

Brughmans has since held onto the No.1 jersey, starting all four of Genk's matches this season.

This includes keeping a clean sheet in their last match - a 4-0 victory against SK Beveren - and has made 15 first-team appearances to date.

4 Aged just 18, Brughmans has already established himself as Genk's No.1 Credit: AFP

As well as impressing at club level, Brughmans has also become a key fixture for Belgium's youth teams and captained his country at the Under-17 European Championship and Under-17 World Cup last year.

He has since gone on to lead their Under-18 and Under-19 teams, and will be hoping a move to Liverpool can put him in the conversation for a senior Belgium call-up.

At present, the Reds' senior goalkeeper options include Mamardashvili, Freddie Woodman and Vitezslav Jaros, alongside Armin Pecsi, who is spending the 2026-27 season on loan at TSV Hartberg.

Sports.title: Oliver Glasner pinches key Crystal Palace star as Nottingham Forest complete £22m deal
Sports.content:
Nottingham Forest have signed Daniel Munoz from Crystal Palace.

Oliver Glasner has reunited with the Colombia right-back at the City Ground before Tuesday's transfer deadline.

3 Forest have signed Munoz for around £22m Credit: Getty

Forest are understood to be paying in the region of £22m for the 30-year-old.

Palace have already strengthened in Munoz's position this summer with two right-sided defenders joining the club.

Oscar Mingueza arrived on a free transfer from Celta Vigo in July.

He was followed through the door at Selhurst Park by Israel international Anan Khalaili earlier this month.

Despite their arrivals, Munoz started at wing-back their defeat to Everton as new manager Pierre Sage operated with a back three.

However, Khalaili and Mingueza shared the role in the loss to Man City.

The 30-year-old joined Palace in January 2024, one month before Glasner's appointment as manager.

Munoz said: "Forest is a team with great players, great qualities and great skills on the pitch, I can’t wait to get out there so I can help my new teammates and I think that we’re going to do great things."

Palace reunion at Forest

His deal at Palace had two years remaining with the option of a further 12 months following an extension in April 2025.

Munoz made 109 appearances across all competitions for the Eagles, scoring 11 goals and adding 16 assists.

Of those, 105 came under Glasner, the fourth most of any player during his Palace tenure.

3 Munoz signed for Palace one month before Glasner was appointed by the club Credit: Getty

During the Austrian's time in charge, Munoz won the FA Cup, Community Shield and Conference League.

However, Glasner departed the club at the end of last season following two-and-a-half years in charge.

He was subsequently appointed Forest manager at the start of July on a three-year deal.

Difficult start for Glasner

The 51-year-old is still awaiting his first victory in charge of the club, though.

Forest began their Premier League campaign with a 1-0 home defeat to Leeds United.

The result was followed by another loss to the same opponents in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday, with Glasner's side booed off at full-time.

3 Glasner is eyeing a reunion with Munoz as he chases his first win as Forest boss Credit: Getty

They then drew 2-2 with Liverpool at Anfield on Saturday.

A move for Munoz would take Forest's summer spending past the £100million barrier.

Club-record signing Liam Delap is their latest addition following his £45million arrival from Chelsea.

Central defender Ousmane Diomande has also joined the club from Sporting Lisbon for £34million.

Sports.content:
The transfer window closes tomorrow and it's sure to be a busy last few hours as several clubs look to make big signings before 11pm. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...
